4edc0b0855d77f7d: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) latest probe into delays in the distribution of Baja 3 to Kedah padi farmers bears similarities to an earlier investigation into an alleged RM1.8 billion padi fertiliser cartel.

The earlier investigation centred on the procurement and supply of fertiliser under a RM1.8 billion government contract awarded to an organisation under a ministry's purview for a 30-month period between 2021 and 2023.

As with the latest Baja 3 investigation, the earlier probe scrutinised the procurement and distribution chain for fertiliser intended for padi farmers, including the role of companies appointed to supply fertiliser and raw materials.

In the earlier case, MACC investigators conducted a series of raids in Kuala Lumpur, including at the organisation's headquarters, the ministry concerned and nine companies which had secured related projects.
Sources had said the organisation was tasked with producing padi fertiliser and distributing it to farmers nationwide through its respective state-level offices.

Investigators found that the organisation had used two methods to fulfil the government contract — purchasing fertiliser directly from five manufacturers and procuring raw materials from another four companies to produce the fertiliser.

The MACC investigation focused on suspected corruption in the procurement of fertiliser or raw materials from selected companies, as well as possible abuse of power involving board members who participated in decisions to appoint companies in which they may have had interests.
Documents related to the project were also seized from the ministry, organisation and companies involved, while six officials from the ministry and organisation were called in for questioning.
Then-MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki confirmed the investigation, which was conducted under Sections 16, 18 and 23 of the MACC Act 2009.

The investigation subsequently led to a former National Farmers Association (Nafas) officer being charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court with two counts of receiving US$300,000 in bribes from a Singaporean fertiliser supplier.

Nordin Ibrohim, 77, was accused of receiving US$200,000 and US$100,000 from Sung Chang Asia Pte Ltd director Kim Jong Kwa as an inducement to help the company secure an appointment as a fertiliser supplier for padi farmers under Nafas.
The alleged payments were made at a bank in Plaza Mont Kiara on Nov 16 and Dec 21, 2022.
Nordin pleaded not guilty to both charges, which were framed under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
The latest investigation, meanwhile, was opened following a complaint lodged by the Malaysian Paddy Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (Pesawah) with Kedah MACC on Aug 26.

MACC said the investigation concerns delays in the distribution of Baja 3 by a supplier appointed by the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry to meet the needs of approximately 100,000ha of padi fields under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada).
Kedah MACC is examining the matter not only for possible criminal offences but also for weaknesses in governance which may have contributed to the delays.
At this stage, however, there has been no indication from MACC that the latest Baja 3 investigation is connected to the earlier RM1.8 billion fertiliser probe.
9a049bdbaf4f43c4: NEW DELHI: Indian rescue teams searched the rubble of a building collapse in New Delhi on Monday, a day after the five-storey block crashed down killing at least six people, officials said.
Emergency teams fear there are people still trapped in in the rubble.
The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), which treated victims from the collapse, said its trauma centre received 10 people.
"Out of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while one patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to his injuries," AIIMS said in a statement.
Disaster agency teams, as well as fire and police teams, are using heavy machinery as well as sniffer dogs to locate anyone who may be trapped.
The Satya Niketan area is home to hundreds of university students living in crowded accommodation.
Building collapses are frequent in India, and illegal structures are common.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the incident was "distressing."
be38f368f7522236: FRANKFURT, Sept 7 — The European Central Bank is expected to raise interest rates again this week as renewed fighting in the Middle East pushes up energy costs and risks further stoking inflation.

Some of the heaviest clashes in weeks in the US-Iran war erupted in recent days, sending oil prices soaring and dimming hopes that energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz will return to normal anytime soon.
Inflation in the 21-nation eurozone, which is heavily dependent on energy imports, hit a three-year high of 3.3 per cent in August, substantially above the ECB’s two-per cent target.
And with fears growing prices will spiral even higher, the central bank is set to hike its benchmark rate for the second time this year when it meets Thursday.
“The ECB governing council looks certain to raise its deposit rate from 2.25 per cent to 2.5 per cent,” said Andrew Kenningham, chief Europe economist at Capital Economics.
The ECB in June delivered its first hike since 2023 to tame surging prices, but then hit pause at its last meeting in July to see how the conflict would develop.

But with Tehran and Washington now seemingly at an impasse, Isabel Schnabel and Joachim Nagel — both members of the ECB’s rate-setting governing council — have signalled in recent days policymakers will resume hiking rates.
The eurozone economy has also proved resilient, growing faster than expected in the second quarter, leaving policymakers with some room to lift borrowing costs without inflicting major damage.
‘Many uncertainties’
The ECB will be armed with fresh growth and inflation forecasts for the next few years to guide its decision, although analysts don’t expect major changes to the projections.
Despite rising inflation, some economists nevertheless believe a rate hike is not the right decision.
“We consider another hike a mistake because there is almost no evidence of knock-on effects,” Felix Schmidt, senior economist at Berenberg bank, told AFP.
“You can’t tackle a supply shock with tighter monetary policy.”
The surge in prices has been almost exclusively driven by energy, and there has been little sign of inflation seeping more broadly into other areas of the economy.
While higher borrowing costs typically help tackle inflation by depressing demand in an economy, observers argue it won’t do much to blunt the impacts of the current oil supply shock.
For Schmidt, the ECB is simply “very worried about being behind the curve because of the experiences of 2021-2022”.

At that time, the central bank faced criticism for moving too slowly as eurozone inflation surged on the back of post-Covid pandemic supply chain woes and then the energy shock from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
However, most analysts expect the ECB to pause its hikes after this week’s meeting.
ECB President Christine Lagarde is, as usual, expected to give little away at her press conference after the rate call and insist that future decisions will be based on incoming data.
ECB council member Nagel, also the head of the German central bank, echoed this cautious stance, saying this week he was “reluctant” to give guidance on future decisions.
“Oil and gas prices keep going up and down. Financial markets are highly volatile. There are many uncertainties,” he told France’s Le Monde newspaper.
“It is an uncomfortable situation — also from a monetary policy perspective. But our meeting-by-meeting approach has served us well in the past and will certainly do so in the future.” — AFP
4fb553329aa1c497: KUANTAN: A nursery staff member has been remanded for six days to facilitate investigations into allegations that she mistreated a 2-year-old boy at a childcare centre here last month.

Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the 31-year-old woman was detained by a team from the Kuantan police headquarters yesterday after a video of the alleged incident went viral on social media.
"So far, only one suspect has been detained for questioning. She has been remanded until Sept 12," he said today.
Yesterday, Kuantan police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the incident was believed to have occurred on Aug 11.
He had said the video showed the victim being scolded, pulled by the hair and having his head shaken by a woman employed at the nursery.

Meanwhile, on an unrelated but similar incident in Temerloh, Azry said police had arrested a 26-year-old woman to facilitate investigations into the alleged mistreatment of a 2-year-old girl by a nursery caretaker.
He said the suspect was detained after the victim's 29-year-old mother lodged a report on Sept 5. The woman has been remanded until Sept 12.

Both cases are being investigated for ill-treatment, neglect, abandonment or exposure of children under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000, imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both.
3a8410ba9e93d5f9: NUUK: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is expected to unveil on Monday a boost in EU investments in Greenland and closer political ties with the Danish Arctic territory, which Donald Trump has insisted should belong to the United States.

Von der Leyen arrived in Greenland on Sunday for a two-day visit serving as a show of support for the governments of Greenland and Denmark, which have strongly rebuffed Trump's campaign to annex the world's largest island.

The head of the 27-nation European Union's executive body, von der Leyen is expected to unveil plans to invest in sectors including critical minerals, satellite communications and renewable energy in Greenland, a semi-autonomous part of the Danish realm.
On Sunday in Nuuk, the capital, von der Leyen said the package would be "substantial" but gave no details.
Greenland Premier Jens-Frederik Nielsen said his country wanted to build on its "close friendship and good partnership" with the EU.

Von der Leyen's visit reflects the increasing geopolitical importance of the Arctic to major powers, such as the United States, Russia, China and Europe, as melting ice opens new shipping routes to make the region's mineral wealth more accessible.

"Greenland's stunning landscapes and natural beauty will stay with me for a long time. But so will the visible scars of climate change on the ice sheet," von der Leyen posted on X after a boat trip under clear blue skies in a fjord scattered with chunks of ice.
"As the ice melts, a new reality is taking shape."

Trump, the US president, sparked a crisis in US-European ties and turmoil within the transatlantic Nato military alliance this year when he stepped up his demands for the US to control Greenland, arguing that fellow Nato member Denmark could not defend it.

European officials stressed Greenland is part of Nato territory, meaning it is covered by the alliance's mutual defence pact, and that the US already has the right to increase its military presence there under a longstanding treaty.

Tensions lowered after Trump and Nato boss Mark Rutte agreed in Davos in January that the United States, Denmark and Greenland would begin talks to resolve their differences and Nato would step up its role in Arctic security.
However, the trilateral talks have yet to yield an agreement and, at a Nato summit in Turkiye in July, Trump restated his insistence that the US should control Greenland.
While Denmark is a member of the EU, Greenland left the bloc in 1985. But its people, as Danish citizens, are also citizens of the EU.
The EU has long provided funding to Greenland, mainly to pay for fishing rights and support its education system.
The package to be announced by von der Leyen will represent not only a big increase in funding but a broadening of the sectors that will receive EU cash, according to EU officials.

0f60f0b44bffcb7e: SEPTEMBER 7 — The graduation ceremony is over. The robe is returned. The mortarboard comes off. A fresh graduate walks out of the university gates, degree in hand and a new question waiting:
“Am I really ready for the world of work?”

In today's rapidly changing Malaysian workplace, employers are looking beyond academic results. They want graduates who can communicate, collaborate, solve problems, adapt to change, think critically and make sound decisions—even when the answer is not found in a textbook.
For years, universities have focused on one fundamental question: What should students know? — Unsplash pic

As Malaysia moves towards a more digital, technology-driven and high-value economy, the expectations placed on fresh graduates are changing. A university degree remains important, but academic qualifications alone may no longer be enough to ensure that graduates are ready to navigate the complexities of the modern workplace.

The Malaysian workforce is entering a period of significant transformation driven by artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, automation and the growth of high-value industries. The Ministry of Human Resources (KESUMA), referring to the World Bank’s 2026 Malaysia Economic Monitor, has emphasised the importance of developing a workforce with skills that are responsive to industry demand, particularly in AI, digitalisation and high-value sectors.

And increasingly, they want something that cannot simply be taught through a lecture which is a “character”. This is where Values-Based Education (VBE) takes centre stage. VBE seeks to integrate values into the learning experience so that students develop not only what they know and can do, but also how they think, behave, and make decisions.
For years, universities have focused on one fundamental question: What should students know?
Today, another question has become equally important:
“What kind of person should a graduate become?”

Therefore, VBE responds to this question by bringing values into the heart of teaching and learning. Students are encouraged to develop not only knowledge and technical competencies, but also integrity, ethics, responsibility, transparency, awareness, empathy and respect.

The philosophy is simple: a graduate should not only know what to do but also understand why it matters and how to do it responsibly. For Malaysia, the goal is therefore no longer simply to produce job-ready graduates but to produce graduates who are future-ready and values-driven. Hence, “Graduation is not the end of learning, but it is the beginning of impact.”
“With knowledge in their minds, skills in their hands and values in their hearts, today's graduates can become the professionals, leaders and changemakers that Malaysia needs tomorrow.”
*Siti Noorjannah Abd Halim is senior lecturer in the Human Resource Management Program, School of Business Management, College of Business, Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM).

ee6e9c0a87fcbed6: WASHINGTON, Sept 7 — US President Donald Trump’s name-changing spree found an unlikely new target yesterday when he suggested the state of New Mexico could become “New America.”

His proposal, which was immediately dismissed by the state’s governor, comes days after he signed an order to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” in the middle of a trade war with neighbouring Canada.

“Many people suggested changing the name of New Mexico... to NEW AMERICA,” the Republican president posted on social media. “So much more prestigious and beautiful for the people of that potentially incredible State. Wow, I Love It!!!”
The White House reposted an image showing the Mexico part of the state’s name crossed out and replaced with “America.”
Some US media reports said the idea originated as an internet hoax.
State governor Michelle Lujan Grisham told Fox News that the name “isn’t up for debate—it’s been ours since before the United States existed.”
She said the president wanted to “distract Americans” from issues such as soaring gas prices.
Trump last week suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz as “Trump Strait” as the war with Iran continues—then hours later implied he was not serious about the plan.
He renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America” on his first day back in the White House in 2025 in a move rejected by Mexico.
Canada has also rejected the attempt to rename Lake Ontario. — AFP
1a3d3b9f584e134a: CYBERJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has been ordered to meet an e-commerce platform believed to have been misused to facilitate the online sale of drugs.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive followed growing concern over the sale of drugs, including fentanyl and a substance known as "piu-piu", online, particularly among youths.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had expressed concern over the trend.

"I have instructed the MCMC to meet one of the platforms that we believe has been involved in the misuse of its network by enabling drugs such as fentanyl or what is known as 'piu-piu' to be sold in Malaysia.

"The MCMC chairman and his team must be fair but firm in dealing with this," he said in his speech at the opening of a strategic cooperation workshop involving the rural community centres under the rural and regional development ministry and the National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) here today.
Also present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Deputy Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang and MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.
Fahmi said efforts to expand internet access, including in rural areas, must be accompanied by measures to ensure communications networks remained secure and were used responsibly.
He said online scams and other forms of abuse could also flourish if digital security and literacy among users were not strengthened.
"We provide good internet access and complement it with PKD and Nadi facilities because we want to bridge the gap between rural, suburban and urban areas.
"However, if these communications networks are not secure and users lack the knowledge or skills to protect themselves, drugs can be sold and distributed everywhere," he said.
aa6f0bbd60af82f8: SEPTEMBER 7 — We have all been there: cruising down the PLUS Expressway or a federal road, only to find ourselves boxed in by towering 40-tonne trailers and cement trucks.
For many Malaysian drivers, it is an anxiety-inducing experience and a recent tragedy on the East Coast Expressway (LPT 1) has once again shown exactly why those fears are justified.
Over a recent six-year period, accidents involving heavy vehicles claimed 1,457 lives in Malaysia. That equates to one death every 36 hours.
The terrifying physics of heavy vehicle accidents became front-page news again on the night of August 31, 2026.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Over a recent six-year period, accidents involving heavy vehicles claimed 1,457 lives in Malaysia. That equates to one death every 36 hours. — Picture by Yusof Mat Isa
Around 10.55pm, at KM110.3 of LPT 1 near Lanchang, Temerloh, a cement tanker lorry lost control and ploughed into a line of slow-moving traffic.
The resulting 11-vehicle pile-up which crushed cars between the cement truck and an express bus claimed four lives.

Tragically, the victims included a young family of three. A 32-year-old husband and wife, along with their four-year-old son, were killed instantly in their Proton S70 as they were making their way home after celebrating National Day in Putrajaya.
This heartbreak highlights a grim statistic: over 80% of fatalities in heavy vehicle crashes are not the truck drivers, but the innocent road users caught in their path.
Beyond the sheer mass of these vehicles, the data reveals deeper systemic issues driving these tragedies.

A study by the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (MIROS) revealed a shocking reality where only 32% of commercial vehicle operators comply with the Industrial Code of Practice for Transport Safety (ICOP).
When fleet maintenance is deferred to save costs, brakes and bald tires fail exactly when they are needed most.

Furthermore, driving massive machinery requires peak alertness, yet the human element remains a vulnerability, with substance abuse casting a persistent shadow over the industry. In early 2026, police reported that 291 heavy vehicle drivers involved in road accidents tested positive for drugs.
Compounding these factors is the deadly combination of speed and weight.

Many heavy vehicles travel at speeds far too fast for their braking capabilities. When carrying illegally overweight cargo, stopping distances multiply exponentially, turning a sudden brake into a fatal rear-end collision, much like the out-of-control cement tanker that could not stop in time during the recent LPT 1 crash.

The good news is that the authorities are not sitting idle, and recent interventions aim to make a significant dent in the mortality rate. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for a thorough investigation into the LPT 1 crash, signalling a push for stricter road safety adherence across the board.

To modernise its approach to road safety, the Ministry of Transport is rolling out High Speed - Weigh in Motion (HS-WIM) technology. Instead of relying on manual roadblocks, this system automatically detects and flags overloaded trucks in real-time as they drive over highway sensors.

Alongside this technological upgrade, the Road Transport Department's (JPJ) recent, uncompromising crackdown on overloaded lorries has yielded tangible results. Preliminary data shows that fatal accidents involving heavy vehicles plummeted from 260 cases in 2024 to just 163 in 2025.

While safety technology and enforcement are improving, the LPT 1 tragedy is a sobering reminder that road safety remains a matter of life and death. The next time you find yourself sharing a lane with a heavy vehicle, remember the physics at play. Give them plenty of braking space, stay entirely out of their massive blind spots, and let the authorities handle the enforcement.

267e74e743baa82f: Kuala Lumpur A never-give-up mentality was one of the keys to the success of the country's Under-20 squad in booking a ticket to the final round of the Asian Cup in China next year.

Technical director of the National Football Development Programme (NFDP) Datuk Ong Kim Swee said that the success deserved credit because it came as a result of the dedication, sacrifice and teamwork shown by the country's young squad throughout the qualification campaign.

He said the determination of the players and coaching staff, led by coach Shukor Adan, to continue fighting until the last action allowed Malaysia to return to the Under-20 Asian Cup after last doing so in 2018.
"Congratulations to the coaching staff led by Shukor Adan and all the players for successfully qualifying for the Under-20 Asian Cup.
"Their dedication, sacrifice and team spirit have finally borne fruit. I am proud of everyone who contributed to this special success," said Kim Swee.
Malaysia secured their place in the finals after closing out their Group H campaign with a 2-1 victory over Laos at the Lao National Stadium in Vientiane on Sunday.
The victory was the first three points for the national squad after previously recording draws against Indonesia and Australia to collect five points.

However, the final match against Laos did not count after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) decided that matches against the bottom team in the group would not bring any points following the Philippines' withdrawal from Group A.

However, the two points collected from the draw with Indonesia and Australia were enough for Malaysia to emerge as one of the seven best runners-up, thus confirming their ticket to the finals in China next year.
Indonesia emerged as Group H champions to also book a ticket to the finals, while Australia, who were also among the favourites, failed to defend their championship after finishing third.
The success of Shukor's team will certainly be a motivational boost to continue improving their performance before facing challenges against the best Asian teams next year from March 24 to April 10.
In the final round, the four best teams that qualify for the semi-finals will earn automatic tickets to the Under-20 World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan next year.
01743ffe21e3c9cc: LETTERS: When we hear about food security, many picture supermarket shelves stocked with rice, vegetables, meat and other essentials. But full shelves do not necessarily mean a food-secure nation.
Food security is about whether people can consistently access sufficient, safe, nutritious and affordable food — today and during times of crisis.
This is at the heart of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG 2), which calls for an end to hunger and all forms of malnutrition while promoting sustainable agriculture.

For Malaysia, achieving zero hunger requires more than ensuring that food is available. It requires a food system that can withstand economic shocks, climate change, supply disruptions and changing consumer needs.

We have a diverse food system, but it remains dependent on imports for several important commodities. Recent national statistics show high import dependency for products such as mutton and beef. Garlic, onions and some fruits are also substantially sourced from overseas.
Such dependence is not automatically a weakness, but it can become a vulnerability when global prices rise, shipping routes are disrupted, or extreme weather affects production.
Malaysia's Food Act 1983 provides an important legal foundation for food safety and consumer protection, supported by the Food Regulations 1985 and Food Hygiene Regulations 2009.

These regulations establish requirements concerning food safety, hygiene, standards, labelling and other aspects of food control. The Food Safety Information System of Malaysia (FoSIM) further supports monitoring and regulatory implementation.
However, food security cannot be achieved through food safety law alone. A food system begins long before food reaches the supermarket.

Agricultural production, fisheries, livestock, food processing, distribution and trade all contribute to whether food remains available and affordable. Laws and policies covering these sectors therefore need to work together, not operate in isolation.

Malaysia's National Agrofood Policy 2021–2030 (NAP 2.0) recognises the need for a sustainable, resilient and tech-driven agrofood sector. More recently, the National Food Security Policy 2030 has placed greater emphasis on strengthening the food system across production, distribution, consumption and food-waste recovery.

Their success ultimately depends on implementation. Farmers, fishermen, livestock producers and food entrepreneurs must be supported not only to produce more, but to produce sustainably and remain economically viable.
Technology can improve productivity, traceability and resource efficiency, but innovation must also be accessible to smaller producers.
At the same time, consumers need better nutrition literacy so that food security is understood not simply as having enough calories, but as having access to safe and nutritious diets.

There is another side to the food-security equation - what happens to the food that we already have. Food that is produced but wasted does not contribute to food security. Reducing household and food-service waste, improving storage and distribution, and finding opportunities to transform food by-products into useful ingredients can help make better use of existing resources.

Ultimately, "availability is not accessibility". Food may be present in markets, yet still be unaffordable or nutritionally inadequate for some households. Thus, zero hunger must be approached through an interconnected framework involving the law, agriculture, economics, nutrition, environmental sustainability and responsible consumption.

Food law can provide the backbone, but agricultural, economic, environmental and social policies must provide the strength to make food security a reality for everyone. The challenge is to connect them effectively.
DR KAMINI SHANMUGAIAH
Head, School of Law Enforcement,
Malaysia University of Science and Technology (MUST)

f4aa6f2999755c22: SEOUL, Sept 7 — Leader Kim Jong Un vowed to build North Korea’s navy into a nuclear-armed force, state media reported today as US allies’ maritime drills were to begin.
This week’s manoeuvres involving Japan, South Korea and the United States were established in 2023 in a response to Pyongyang’s missile and nuclear threats.
Kim spoke at the commissioning of the Kang Kon — a warship that partially capsized when launched in May 2025 — in the port city of Wonsan yesterday, the official Korean Central News Agency reported.

“We should make sure that the diversified and effective operation of nuclear combat systems is conducted for an actual war through developing our navy into a nuclear armed force,” Kim reportedly told the ceremony.
“Once ordered anytime, the new-generation destroyer should deal a deadly retaliatory blow at the enemies as it is a force involved in the state nuclear counteraction system,” he said.
Photos released of Kim showed him accompanied by his daughter, Ju Ae, who is reportedly designated as a successor to her father.
Kim oversaw in July a test of the Kang Kon — one of two 5,000-tonne class warships launched last year — just over a year after it was damaged during its launch.
This week’s US allies’ drills, dubbed Freedom Edge, are set to run to Friday in international waters east and south of South Korea’s Jeju Island.
The manoeuvres have pushed ahead despite President Donald Trump curtailing another set of drills with South Korea as the US leader aims to reopen diplomacy with Pyongyang about its nuclear programme.
Seoul and Washington wrapped up last month Ulchi Freedom Shield, which Trump had ordered scaled back — cutting it from 11 days to five — citing high costs and his good relationship with Kim.

Despite Trump’s overtures, North Korea has shown little sign of reciprocating, firing missiles and condemning the downsized drills as well as Washington’s approval of arms sales to South Korea and plans to fund programmes documenting human rights abuses in the North.
Pyongyang has repeatedly declared itself an “irreversible” nuclear state since a 2019 summit between Kim and Trump in Hanoi collapsed over the scope of denuclearisation and sanctions relief. — AFP
189709d4ef6f17f4: KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to lift the emergency declaration in Serian, Sarawak, which was imposed following worsening haze conditions.
The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) said the consent was given following advice from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and consultations with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
It said the relevant agency had confirmed that the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in Serian had dropped below hazardous levels.
A check of the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website today showed that Serian's API stood at 211, which is classified as very unhealthy.
"However, the haze situation in Sarawak has not fully recovered.
"API readings in several areas, particularly Serian and Samarahan, remain at very unhealthy levels," PMO said in a statement.
PMO said Putrajaya and the Sarawak government will continue to monitor the situation closely.
"Residents in affected areas are strongly advised to limit outdoor activities and strictly adhere to directives issued by the authorities," it said.
On Sept 4, Sultan Ibrahim consented to the declaration of an emergency in Serian following worsening haze conditions, with the API reaching a hazardous level of 521 during the period.
867d431719d350fe: PETALING JAYA: An unemployed man who was uncontactable for three days was found dead in his rented room in Padang Matsirat, Langkawi, yesterday.

Langkawi police chief Khairul Azhar Nuruddin said the landlord was alerted by the man's cousin at about 6.55pm. The cousin was concerned as she had been unable to reach him for several days, Kosmo reported.
"After several unanswered calls, the landlord peered through the window, saw the victim lying motionless on the bed and called the police," he was quoted as saying.
Khairul said initial checks found no signs of a struggle or physical injuries on the man's body.
"There were no indicators of foul play, and the victim had no known history of medical conditions," he said.
The victim was identified as Khairol Iqmal Rohidin, 37, from Kangar, Perlis. His remains were sent to the forensic unit at Sultanah Maliha Hospital for an autopsy.
The case has been classified as sudden death.
facf3266b49c8a9c: PETALING JAYA: Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim has consented to end the emergency declared in Serian, Sarawak, over the haze situation.

The Prime Minister’s Office said the Agong gave his consent after taking into account the advice of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg, as well as agency reports showing that the air pollutant index (API) reading in Serian was no longer at a hazardous level.
“However, the haze in Sarawak has not fully dissipated, and API readings in several areas, particularly in Serian and Samarahan, are at very unhealthy levels,” it said in a statement.
It said the federal and state governments would continue monitoring the situation.
"Residents in the affected areas are advised to limit outdoor activities and comply with the authorities’ directions," it said.
The state of emergency was declared in Serian last Friday after haze pushed the API reading into the hazardous range.

As of noon today, the Air Pollutant Index Management System portal showed Samarahan and Serian in Sarawak as the only areas in the country with very unhealthy air quality, with API readings of 236 and 222 respectively.
Unhealthy API readings were recorded in 36 areas, while 22 had moderate readings and one had a good reading.

Sarawak remained the worst-hit state, with nine areas recording unhealthy air quality: Sarikei (197), Kuching (193), Sibu (185), Sri Aman (183), Mukah (182), Bintulu and ILP Miri (169 each), Miri (166) and Limbang (138).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and above 300, hazardous.
a30bb3ae9b877504: JOHOR BARU: Haze tightened its grip on Johor today, with four districts recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
Segamat and Batu Pahat recorded the highest readings at 157, followed by Tangkak (154) and Kluang (151), according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
Readings between 101 and 200 are classified as unhealthy, while readings between 201 and 300 are considered very unhealthy and those above 300 hazardous.

The deterioration in air quality has prompted Johor to tighten precautions at schools, with state Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali saying schools would be closed if API readings exceeded 200.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecasted haze across Johor today and tomorrow, with temperatures reaching 35 degrees Celcius.
Isolated thunderstorms are forecasted from Wednesday, although haze is expected to persist at night.
The latest readings showed Johor was not the worst-hit state, with Samarahan, Sarawak recording the country's only very unhealthy reading at 226. Nationwide, 40 areas recorded unhealthy API readings.
Isolated thunderstorms are forecasted from Wednesday, although the haze is expected to persist at night.

The haze comes amid continued hot and dry conditions and regional fires, with smoke from hotspots in Indonesia's Sumatra and Kalimantan affecting parts of southern Peninsular Malaysia.
a385fa4d64c311aa: JAKARTA, Sept 7 — Jakarta’s main airport and three others extended their closure to 6pm today after being forced to halt operations due to a volcanic eruption, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded.
Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150 kilometres from Indonesia’s capital, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and plume of volcanic ash.

Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting hundreds of flights and leaving more than 170,000 passengers stranded, according to the transport ministry.

At least four airports, including Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, extended their closure from this morning to 6pm (1100 GMT/7pm Malaysian time), airport operator Angkasa Pura said in a social media post.

“In connection with the increasing eruption activity of Mount Anak Krakatau, flight operations at several airports have been suspended; passengers are advised to regularly monitor their flight status with the respective airlines,” the operator said.
Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller airport that caters to both civil and military flights, also extended its closure, the company said.
The probability of an eruption remains high until this morning, the country’s geology agency said.

“The threat from an eruption comes from the ejection of incandescent rocks accompanied by heavy ashfall. Another potential hazard arises from lava flows if the eruption resumes and continues,” the agency said.
Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and left thousands displaced. — AFP
a707b7a984ca7d39: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — As Malaysia’s paddy farmers grapple with delays in subsidised fertiliser supplies, one of the country’s key agricultural organisations is undergoing a major overhaul after years of financial losses.

Pertubuhan Peladang Kebangsaan (Nafas) – the national farmers’ organisation that supports agricultural cooperatives and distributes farm inputs – is shutting nine of its 16 subsidiaries and refocusing on agricultural inputs, its core business which accounts for more than 95 per cent of its revenue.

The restructuring comes as the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission investigates delays in the distribution of supplementary compound fertiliser affecting about 38,000 paddy farmers in Kedah’s Muda Agricultural Development Authority area.

Nafas itself is not implicated in that investigation, but its renewed focus on agricultural inputs puts the organisation at the centre of a business that is critical to farmers and heavily dependent on government support.

Nafas general manager Muhammad Faris Arriffin told Berita Harian that the organisation’s restructuring was driven by the financial position it inherited when its current management took over in March 2023.
“When we took over the leadership of Nafas in March 2023, Nafas recorded net losses and had debts of more than RM400 million in the 2022 financial year,” he was quoted as saying.

Nafas general manager Muhammad Faris Ariffin disclosed that the national farmers’ organisation is shutting nine of its 16 subsidiaries and refocusing on agricultural inputs as part of its restructuring drive. — Bernama pic
The turnaround strategy involves closing nine subsidiaries involved in non-core businesses and concentrating resources on areas that can deliver greater value to farmer members and the government.
Nafas’s agricultural-input business includes the distribution of fertiliser and other farm supplies, with government fertiliser contracts worth up to RM2 billion a year.
The organisation’s six remaining subsidiaries are focused on its core businesses, with four involved in fertiliser, pesticides and other agricultural inputs, while two are in the palm oil industry.
9a6b98d7e4ab19a1: PETALING JAYA: Pengisytiharan darurat bagi seluruh bahagian Serian, Sarawak yang diisytiharkan tiga hari lalu susulan keadaan jerebu ditamatkan hari ini selepas bacaan Indeks Pencemaran Udara (IPU) tidak lagi berada di paras bahaya.

Pejabat Perdana Menteri memaklumkan penamatan itu mendapat perkenan Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim setelah mengambil kira nasihat Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim dan pandangan Premier Sarawak Abang Johari Openg.
"Bagaimanapun, keadaan jerebu di Sarawak masih belum pulih sepenuhnya dan bacaan IPU di beberapa kawasan, khususnya Serian dan Samarahan, masih berada pada tahap amat tidak sihat.

"Kerajaan persekutuan dan kerajaan Sarawak akan terus memantau keadaan dengan rapi dan penduduk di kawasan terjejas dinasihatkan supaya mengehadkan aktiviti di luar rumah serta sentiasa mematuhi arahan pihak berkuasa," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Setakat 9 pagi hari ini, hanya Samarahan mencatatkan tahap kualiti udara sangat tidak sihat iaitu 230, manakala Serian pula merekodkan IPU 195 iaitu bacaan tidak sihat.
Pada Jumaat lalu, seluruh bahagian Serian diisytiharkan darurat selepas IPU mencapai 515, melepasi tahap bahaya iaitu 301 ke atas berikutan jerebu rentas sempadan akibat kebakaran hutan di Indonesia.
Darurat jerebu kali terakhir diisytiharkan di Kuching pada September 1997, apabila bacaan IPU mencecah 650.
1e87feeae44ce38b: GERIK: Eight members of the Perak Fire and Rescue Department's Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (Storm) team have been deployed to search for six people reported missing after joining the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan.
The team, accompanied by five firemen, will travel by boat from Trojan Jetty to Pos Kemar, where they will assemble before beginning the search operation.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Sayani Saidon said three boats had been deployed at Trojan Jetty to facilitate the movement of the rescue personnel.

She said the department received information about the group's disappearance yesterday afternoon and subsequently held a coordination meeting with its Operations Division before deciding to launch the search this morning.
"The missing group comprises two mountain guides and a family of four.
"We have eight Storm personnel and five firemen who will travel from Trojan Jetty to Pos Kemar, where we will assemble," she said.

Sayani said 12 Mountain Guides Association (MGP) members from the Forestry Department had also departed from Sungai Siput by four-wheel-drive vehicles and were expected to take about four hours to reach Pos Kemar.
She said an inter-agency coordination meeting was still being held at the Gerik police headquarters to finalise the deployment of rescue teams and the search and rescue (SAR) operation.
"A forward control post will be established at Pos Kemar, while the main command post will likely be set up at the Gerik police headquarters. However, this has yet to be finalised," she said.
Sayani said the department's K9 unit had arrived this morning and was on standby to assist in the search if required.
"For now, we are holding off on deploying the K9 unit until we obtain more concrete information and finalise the search plan," she said.
Meanwhile, she said the department's air unit was scheduled to depart from Bertam in Penang at 2pm today to conduct an aerial survey.
She said the initial aerial search would begin from the group's last known location on Sept 1 before proceeding towards Pos Kemar.

"The aerial survey will be the initial phase of the operation," she said adding that the SAR operation involved several agencies, including the police, Forestry Department, the Fire and Rescue Department, General Operations Force and mountain guides.
She said additional personnel and agencies could be deployed depending on developments and operational requirements.
It was reported yesterday that six people were uncontactable after joining the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah in the Lojing Permanent Forest Reserve in Gua Musang.
The group, comprising a married couple, their two children, and two mountain guides, began their trek on Aug 29.
50e145f75b247185: SEOUL: BLACKPINK's Lisa has opened up about the restrictions she faced as a K-Pop star, including keeping past relationships private because she feared they could affect the group's popularity.
"In K-Pop culture, we can't date," Lisa says in her upcoming documentary 'Always Lalisa', according to recent Canadian media reports.
"If you're seeing someone and you get caught by paparazzi, your popularity drops," she says.
"When I was younger, I had a few relationships, but we had to hide when we're dating. I didn't want my dating to be the thing that hurts BLACKPINK's popularity."
Lisa also reflects on the pressures she experienced after moving to South Korea from Thailand in 2011 at the age of 14 to begin training under YG Entertainment.
"I finally get to live my life," she says in the documentary. "I didn't dare speak up or express my thoughts, and I had been living like that since I was 14."

The documentary captures Lisa becoming emotional as she recalls her trainee years, including the monthly performance tapes she was required to submit for evaluation and the feedback she received during her training.
She also reveals that 'Dream', a track from her 2025 solo album 'Alter Ego', was inspired by one of the relationships she had kept private.
Lisa said she sought the person's permission before releasing the song, with the condition that their identity would remain undisclosed.
"They thought they figured it out, but I don't think so," Lisa says, referring to fans who attempted to identify the person behind the song.
Directed by Sue Kim, 'Always Lalisa' follows Lisa over a year as she pursues solo music, acting and other projects outside BLACKPINK.
The documentary will premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on Sept 11, before opening in IMAX and cinemas worldwide from Oct 12 and later streaming on YouTube Premium in 2026.
2dd61796b623e505: KUALA LUMPUR: Solar adoption is expected to gain momentum amid higher electricity bills stemming from the Middle East conflict, said RHB Research.
The firm said the government had imposed an automatic fuel adjustment surcharge of 3.67 sen per kilowatt-hour (kWh) for September.
As a result, average monthly electricity bills increased by 12 per cent compared with pre-war levels, when consumers received a 2.77 sen per kWh rebate.
"We believe the higher tariffs will drive solar power adoption, benefiting the solar engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning players," it said in a note.

Meanwhile, RHB Research said the energy sector's first-half 2026 (1H26) earnings were broadly in line with expectations, with one of the 10 energy companies under its coverage outperforming, six meeting expectations and three falling short.
It said the earnings of large-cap companies with market capitalisation of at least RM2 billion were broadly in line with expectations.
Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) recurring earnings for 1H26 rose five per cent year-on-year (YoY), supported by a nine per cent increase in electricity unit sales.
"Growth was mainly driven by the commercial sector, which captures electricity sales to data centres.
"TNB's effective tax rate (ETR) also narrowed to 28 per cent in the second quarter 2026 – management is maintaining its target to achieve 23 to 24 per cent ETR for the full year," RHB Research said.
Meanwhile, YTL Power International Bhd reported earnings that were in line with the firm's expectations but exceeded consensus estimates, driven by a strong contribution from its data centre segment.

The segment contributed RM244 million to the group in the fourth quarter of financial year 2026 (Q4 FY26), up significantly from RM59 million in Q3 FY26, on the back of full utilisation of its 150 megawatt (MW) operating capacity.

"We expect data centre contribution to accelerate further as YTL Power is on track to complete another 200MW capacity by June 2027. YTL Power also recently acquired 58.7 hectares of land to build another one gigawatt capacity in Sedenak," it said.
RHB Research maintained its "Overweight" stance on the energy sector, with YTL Power remaining its top pick.

"YTL Power is set to benefit from rising data centre capacity, while TNB is the prime beneficiary of the National Energy Transition Roadmap, with the regulated framework providing a stable earnings base," it said.
The firm also favoured Samaiden Group Bhd and Solarvest Holdings Bhd, which it said were positioned to benefit from new solar tenders.
77fa3b9beb50d882: SEOUL: China could see recent cuts to US-South Korean military exercises as an opportunity to reassert itself in the Indo-Pacific, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said on Monday, though he said Washington had assured Manila that its commitments to the Philippines remained unchanged.

Speaking to Reuters on the sidelines of the Seoul Defense Dialogue, Teodoro said there had been no reduction in US-Philippine military activities and that bilateral and multilateral cooperation involving Manila continued to expand.

US President Donald Trump's decision last month to scale back military exercises with South Korea has prompted debate among security analysts over the credibility of US deterrence in Asia and whether rivals such as China could perceive a weakening of US resolve.
"It is a possibility, of course. China is very quick to exploit gaps," Teodoro said when asked whether Beijing could seize on the move.
"If we're talking about the Indo-Pacific as a whole, then it may signal some opportunity for China to reassert itself," he said.

Teodoro said, however, that Manila had received "definite assurances" from Washington and that there was "no indication" that the changes in South Korea would affect commitments under the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty.

Manila has deepened defence cooperation with the US under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., including expanded joint exercises and greater access for US forces to Philippine military facilities, as tensions with China have intensified in the South China Sea.

Teodoro said Manila was also broadening security ties with other partners. The Philippines recently concluded agreements with Canada and New Zealand, signed a visiting forces agreement with France, and was negotiating a similar pact with Britain, he said.
The defence chief also accused China of relying increasingly on influence operations alongside military and maritime pressure.
"Definitely it takes advantage of democratic space in order to co-opt people and to use a free media to expand its distortive narratives," he said.
Teodoro said the Philippines was pursuing stronger espionage and foreign influence legislation to counter such activities.

Asked about Marcos' recent remarks that progress was being made toward possible joint oil and gas exploration talks with China, Teodoro struck a cautious note, saying it would be "doubtful" that any economic cooperation could be insulated from longstanding sovereignty disputes in the South China Sea.
China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Teodoro's remarks.
Teodoro was in Seoul for talks aimed at expanding defence cooperation with South Korea, one of the Philippines' largest arms suppliers.
South Korea has supplied the Philippines with FA-50 light combat aircraft, frigates and other military equipment as Manila modernises its armed forces.

He said the Philippines was interested in deeper industrial cooperation and emerging defence technologies from South Korea, but indicated that a long-discussed submarine acquisition programme remained some way off.

"The submarine program is still under review," he said, citing questions over mission requirements and the substantial infrastructure needed to support such a capability. "I would say it will be still a way off."

Teodoro said concerns about China's actions were encouraging closer security cooperation among countries across the region and could ultimately lead to a more interconnected Indo-Pacific security network.
"I believe so because the motivating factor there is China," he said.

3ffb2b15588b9bc6: KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of AirAsia Group Bhd and Capital A Bhd came under selling pressure on Monday after reports that the Finance Ministry has appointed an adviser to assess the aviation group's funding requirements.
At 11.11am, Capital A fell 1.5 sen or 4.84 per cent to 29.5 sen, with 29.69 million shares changing hands, making it the fifth most actively traded counter on Bursa Malaysia.
The stock opened at 31 sen and fell to an intraday low of 28.5 sen, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM1.32 billion.

AirAsia Group, meanwhile, declined 3.5 sen or 4.96 per cent to 67 sen, with 15.66 million shares traded. It opened at 70 sen and touched an intraday low of 65.5 sen. The counter was the ninth most actively traded stock on the exchange.
At 67 sen, the company had a market capitalisation of RM2.25 billion.

The sell-off came after Reuters reported on Sept 3 that the Finance Ministry had hired an adviser to assess the aviation company's funding needs, signalling that the government is weighing potential support for the airline group.
According to the report, considerations include the public interest and the wider economic impact of the aviation company.
The development comes as AirAsia Group is pursuing fundraising exercises comprising up to US$1 billion in international debt markets and RM700 million in local credit facilities.

In a statement on Sept 2, the group said the fundraising was primarily aimed at debt restructuring, refinancing and balance sheet consolidation, rather than solely addressing operational funding shortfalls.
It said the strategy was in line with its previously announced plans to optimise its capital structure.

The group said it had successfully raised about US$300 million in March 2026, despite heightened global market volatility and fuel price uncertainty, to extend debt maturities and reduce principal obligations.
It said the latest funding strategy was aimed at consolidating multiple existing facilities into a single, lower-cost debt structure with longer maturities and more favourable terms.
The exercise would also enable the group to refinance higher-cost debt incurred during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Year to date, Capital A's share price has fallen 28.04 per cent, while AirAsia Group has declined 62.7 per cent.
b76fa297f94a6399: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the youth to stop merely waiting for the future to unfold and instead shape the country's destiny through knowledge, conviction, courage and strong values.
He said the younger generation should be willing to challenge convention while remaining mindful of the needs and well-being of others.
"I am confident that before me are the faces of the great generation we are building to lead tomorrow," he said.

Anwar said this in his speech, which was read out by Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang at the National Science Challenge final for the Prime Minister's Challenge Trophy here today.
Anwar said Malaysia's future depended on a generation that was knowledgeable, resilient and willing to take responsibility for shaping the country's direction.
He said scientific and technological progress must also move in tandem with human values under the Malaysia Madani framework.
"Science without compassion can become cold; innovation without integrity can become dangerous; and knowledge without courage will remain only in reports," he said.
He said Malaysia needed three qualities — creativity, confidence and compassion — to ensure scientific and technological development benefited society.

Anwar said the National Science Challenge was not merely a competition to determine who knew the most facts, but a platform to develop the courage to think, work as a team, test ideas, defend evidence and learn from failure.
He called on participants not to fear failure, saying it was part of the process of finding answers in science.
"If an experiment does not succeed, do not see it as a failure that breaks your spirit. In science, failure is part of the process of finding an answer," he said.
Anwar said the participants could go on to become scientists, doctors, engineers, researchers, teachers, technology entrepreneurs or leaders in fields that did not yet exist.
He urged them to carry their curiosity, courage to experiment and sense of responsibility to benefit others, regardless of the careers they eventually chose.
He also stressed that scientific and technological progress must go hand in hand with humanity and integrity.

"Creativity requires us to imagine something new. Confidence requires us to test it. Compassion requires us to keep asking who benefits, who may be left behind, and whether the solution we produce truly improves people's lives," he said.
3518d9db4068e788: KUALA LUMPUR: Melwood Boys FC of Kuala Lumpur showed grit and determination to retain the UKRC Soccer 9s title after edging Penang Sports Club 6-5 on penalties after a scoreless draw at the UKRC field on Sunday.
The match was a repeat of last year's final, which Melwood Boys won 1-0.
This year's decider was much tighter, with the teams deadlocked after regulation time. Both teams then opted to proceed directly to a penalty shootout instead of playing extra-time.
There were only seven teams in this year's competition, forcing the organisers to adopt a single round-robin format instead of the traditional two-group format.

"It's great to retain the title, especially under the new rule this year that allowed teams to field three players aged 45 to 49, instead of the traditional over-50s format," said Melwood Boys president M. Hari Chandran.
"In the end, we decided to field only one younger player, and the move paid off as we retained the crown with a hard-fought victory.
"It was not easy as Penang Sports Club only had two matches before the final, so they had a longer rest period today. However, they did most of their work the day before."

Penang Sports Club were the only unbeaten team after the group stage, winning five and drawing one of their six matches. One of their victories came against Melwood Boys, whom they beat 2-1 with a last-minute goal.
The Penang outfit played four times on the first day and twice before the final, while Melwood Boys had three league matches on each day.
Melwood Boys pocketed RM3,000 for their victory, while Penang Sports Club received RM1,500.
Meanwhile, in the Plate final, Interact Recreation Club of Negri Sembilan edged hosts UKRC 5-4 after the teams agreed to go straight to penalties.
Bangkok Bitcoin of Thailand won the Fair Play Trophy, the K. Suppiah Memorial Trophy, named after the founder of UKRC.
Interact's Ben Edo Osagie was the tournament's top scorer with 12 goals, earning the Uncle Lee Memorial Trophy.

1a2a014f0773cf9c: HONG KONG, Sept 7 — Tech firms rallied on a mixed day for Asian stocks today, with traders gearing up for a crucial week of events culminating in US inflation data that could determine the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates.
The gains — led by chipmakers in Seoul and Tokyo — came even after a forecast-busting reading on US jobs Friday that ramped up bets the central bank will tighten monetary policy on September 16.
A fresh bout of tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes at the weekend pushed oil higher and added upward pressure to inflation expectations.
After July’s rout of AI-linked firms, dealers have been edging back into the sector, confident that the vast sums invested in recent years will pay off — despite concerns about elevated valuations.

The latest boost came after ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said last week it would begin rolling out its newest and most powerful artificial intelligence model to select customers, saying it had built in safeguards to mitigate security risks.
The firm sees GPT-6, also known as Astra, as a crucial part of a decade-long push towards artificial general intelligence — tools as clever as humans.
Investors are also looking forward to the release of earnings from tech titan Oracle on Thursday. The release will be pored over for a fresh idea about the outlook for the AI boom.
South Korea’s Samsung and SK hynix soared four and six per cent respectively, while Kioxia, Tokyo Electron and Advantest rallied between five and 7.5 per cent in Japan.

On broader markets, Seoul was more than three per cent higher and Tokyo added more than two per cent, with Taipei up more than one per cent thanks to a spike in chipmaker TSMC. There were also gains in Sydney and Jakarta.
However, Hong Kong, Singapore, Wellington and Manila fell, while Shanghai was flat.

“Markets may look calm on the surface, but the combination of central-bank meetings, US inflation, Oracle earnings and flows in China tech suggests the conditions for a more meaningful expansion in volatility are building as the week progresses,” said Chris Weston at Pepperstone.
Friday’s release of the US consumer price index for August is seen as critical in deciding whether the Fed hikes rates next week or stands put.
The CME Group’s FedWatch tool put the chances of an increase at more than 56 per cent after figures Friday showed the US economy created far more jobs than expected in August.
Elias Haddad, at Brown Brothers Harriman, said: “A September 16 Fed funds rate hike hinges on Friday’s US August CPI print.
“A hot CPI print would all but seal a September hike and underpin a firmer US dollar. A cooler reading would strengthen the case for a hold.”

While data put pressure on the Fed to lift rates, the yen held last week’s healthy gains against the dollar amid speculation the Bank of Japan will hike borrowing costs at each of its next two meetings.
The likelihood that rates will rise has seen yields on government bonds around the world rise, and comes as the Middle East war continues with no sign of ending.
Iran’s top negotiator threatened Sunday a more forceful response to any further US attacks following strikes on American warships in their latest round of clashes.
The exchanges of fire, which began with US raids last week, come amid a deadlock in the six-month conflict.
The spike in oil prices sent US diesel prices to a record high of US$5.85 a gallon last week.

d279f591bf393ac9: KUALA LUMPUR: Dua penerbangan ke Jakarta dilencongkan ke KLIA susulan letusan gunung berapi Anak Krakatau, kata Pihak Berkuasa Penerbangan Awam Malaysia (CAAM).

e0d5076a545d7a3c: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said a newly commissioned destroyer would be part of a nuclear response system capable of delivering "annihilating retaliatory strikes", state media KCNA reported on Monday, though it did not say whether the vessel would carry nuclear weapons.
North Korea has accelerated efforts to modernise its navy as Kim pursues a broader expansion of the country's nuclear-capable forces.
At a commissioning ceremony in the port city of Wonsan on Sunday, Kim said deploying the new ship to the sea east of the Korean Peninsula sent a clear signal to North Korea's adversaries.
"The time has come for us to exercise our sovereignty at sea and underwater," Kim said, according to KCNA.

Kim's daughter, known as Ju Ae, took a prominent role in the ceremony, wearing a white dress suit, standing beside her father to receive salutes, appearing on a giant screen above the cheering crowd and boarding the destroyer, KCNA photographs showed.
Seoul's ​National Intelligence Service (NIS) believes that North Korea is continuing to ​take steps to position Ju Ae as Kim's ‌successor, a South Korean lawmaker said last week.

The 5,000-tonne-class destroyer, the "Kang Kon", is the second warship of its class to enter service, following the commissioning of the "Choe Hyon" destroyer on North Korea's west coast about three months earlier, KCNA cited Kim as saying.

Kim said North Korea's naval nuclear armaments were advancing, and the country would continue to expand what he called its most powerful strategic assets in key waters to protect its maritime sovereignty and regional security.
He added that the Kang Kon would form part of North Korea's state nuclear response system.

"Kim's remarks are a public declaration that the destroyers will be used as platforms for sea-based nuclear deterrence," said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University's Institute for Far Eastern Studies.
"The Kang Kon's deployment to the sea to the east of the Peninsula is intended to deter US, South Korean and Japanese naval operations near the peninsula."
South Korea, the United States and Japan began their annual "Freedom Edge" exercise on Monday in international waters southeast and south of Jeju Island, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said.

The drill running until Friday involves major maritime and air assets from the three countries and is intended to strengthen deterrence and response capabilities against North Korea's nuclear and missile threats, the JCS said.
KCNA did not specify what weapons systems might be deployed on the Kang Kon, but said it carried the same systems as the Choe Hyon.
A previous KCNA report said Choe Hyon-class destroyers can carry a range of weapons, including missiles that analysts say are capable of carrying a nuclear payload.
Kim said North Korea would demonstrate another stage of its naval buildup in eight months, KCNA reported, without giving details.
"The eight-month timetable may signal the coming disclosure of another major strategic asset, rather than simply another surface warship," Lim said.
South Korea's Unification Ministry said Seoul would closely monitor developments and noted that nuclear armament of North Korea's navy has been discussed since the Ninth Party Congress in February.
Kim also said the construction of naval bases on North Korea's east coast was underway and that the country would create new naval units and build different classes of warships.
