7525f10036c6e294: RAUB: A civil servant lost RM151,967 after falling victim to a love scam involving a suspect posing as a project manager based in Türkiye.
The woman even took out a bank loan after being tricked by the suspect, who claimed the money was needed to ensure the continuity of his projects abroad and cover his personal expenses.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman said the victim befriended the 'foreigner' in April before she was told to transfer money to assist him in stages.
"The suspect told the victim that his bank account had been frozen and that he needed money to manage his projects and for his own use.
"The victim used her savings and took out a bank loan to assist the suspect.
"She made 35 transactions amounting to RM151,967 into 10 separate unknown bank accounts between April 22 and Aug 26 this year," he said in a statement today.
Shahril said the victim realised she had fallen victim to a love scam after the suspect blocked her on social media and lodged a police report at the district police headquarters at 6pm yesterday.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Members of the public are advised to conduct checks at https://semakmule.rmp.gov.my before carrying out any transaction.
1e41f835e9fce788: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — A helicopter search for 17 Malaysians who have been missing nearly two weeks since flash floods hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district has found no trace of the group, their belongings or the six vehicles they were travelling in.
Fishtail Tours & Travels representative Roshan Panday said the helicopter made four passes over the area where the vehicles were swept away but found nothing, The New Straits Times reported today.
“It seems the current was at maximum power when it reached that particular spot,” he told the newspaper.
Roshan said several houses had stood near the site, but the force of the floodwaters had left no visible remains of the buildings.
The search team also checked a nearby forest, although it appeared unlikely that the group had managed to reach the area, he said.
The helicopter then flew at low altitude along a 30km stretch downstream from the site but found nothing believed to belong to the missing group.
Meanwhile, the agency split its office team into three groups to search hospitals for any injured members of the group, but none had been found.
The team also checked bodies recovered from the disaster, but none had so far been positively identified as members of the group.
“Search is still on,” Roshan was quoted as saying.
People help a vehicle navigate a damaged, muddy road leading to remote Rasuwa after flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 4, 2026. — AFP pic
The group was travelling in six vehicles carrying 27 tourists, including 17 Malaysians, two Americans and a Briton.
They were accompanied by seven Nepali crew members, including a doctor who volunteered to provide medical support to the 20 tourists travelling to high altitude.
Six drivers were also part of the convoy, bringing the total number of people involved to 33.
The 17 Malaysians have remained uncontactable since flash floods struck Rasuwa – among the worst hit areas – with search efforts continuing to locate them.
Roshan said on September 1 that the agency would deploy a private helicopter to search for the missing Malaysians.
05e69203db66028e: NEW YORK: A quarter century after the era-defining attacks of Sept 11, the United States is eager to keep alive the memory of a 2001 trauma that is fading as the proportion of Americans who did not experience it firsthand grows.

President Donald Trump will pay his respects at the Pentagon rather than in New York, where the attacks by hijacked passenger planes on the World Trade Center towers claimed the largest number of the 2,977 total victims recorded on that day.

But vice president JD Vance and Trump's four living predecessors - Democrats Joe Biden, Barack Obama and Bill Clinton, as well as Republican George Bush, who was president at the time of the attacks - are all expected at the "Ground Zero" site in lower Manhattan next Friday.
The anniversary commemorates a watershed moment for the US and the world.
"Many in my generation remember exactly where we were on that horrific day" in 2001, said Beth Hillman, 59, president of the 9/11 Memorial & Museum and a US Air Force veteran.
Yet today, "100 million Americans were not even born or are too young to remember" the tragic events.
'More inquisitive' young people

After placing major emphasis on the duty to remember, her institution is now focusing on outreach, education and engaging younger generations. Trained volunteers, including first responders, connect with audiences who have learned of the disaster solely through their parents or school.

"Even if you were alive but not here or have a connection, it's a lot easier to understand the magnitude of what took place," Logan Miller, a 32-year-old who lost an uncle and a grandfather as a result of the attacks, told AFP.
Making sense of 9/11 is "a little tougher for that next generation," he added.
Miller is one of many volunteers sharing their experiences at the museum, which gets 2.4 million unique visitors per year, or through video clips.
Young people are "more inquisitive" and ask more questions than their elders, who Miller said sometimes hesitate to challenge him for fear of causing offence.

"I wasn't born at the time and yet it was important for me to be here, to do this trip," said 22-year-old Ignacio Gaete, a Chilean visiting the museum and memorial featuring two large recessed pools within the footprints of the Twin Towers.
Gaete said that while young people don't have visceral memories of 9/11 like his father does, "I think it can transcend generations."
But that transcendence requires preservation and education, according to Holly Kafka, visiting Manhattan from Chicago with her husband.
"Our younger generation... they're always in this little rat race, keeping up with social media," the 61-year-old said. "We have to stop them and say, 'Come here and experience it.'"
9,400 more deaths

As they do every year at Ground Zero starting at 8.40am (1240 GMT), the time shortly before hijacked American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower, relatives will read the long list of their loved ones' names.
In the evening, two beams of light will project skyward from lower Manhattan, symbolic of the towers.
Nineteen Al-Qaeda operatives hijacked four planes on that nearly cloudless day in 2001. Two jets slammed into the World Trade Center, causing the iconic 110-story buildings to collapse.

A third plane struck the Pentagon, while a fourth - which apparently had targeted the US Capitol or the White House - crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers fought back.
Beyond those killed on Sept 11, more than 9,400 other people have died from 9/11-related illnesses, according to the federal programme established to provide medical care to those affected.

The trial of Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, alleged mastermind of the attacks and a top lieutenant of al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden, was recently scheduled for June 2028 at the US Navy base in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. He has been detained there for 20 years.
Trump, 80, has confirmed he will skip the Ground Zero event and instead speak at the Pentagon on 9/11.

The New York Times reported it was because Trump would not be allowed to deliver remarks at the site, which has strictly banned speeches so commemorations there could remain nonpartisan. The president dismissed the reporting as "made up."
de24dad342e45b7b: KUALA LUMPUR: Two Jakarta-bound flights were diverted to KLIA following the eruption of Anak Krakatau, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said today.
CAAM CEO Norazman Mahmud said Malaysia was assisting Indonesia by allowing KLIA to serve as an alternative airport.

"Some aircraft bound for Jakarta have been diverted to KLIA. So far, we have received two diverted flights," he said on the sidelines of the 61st Conference of Directors-General of Civil Aviation for the Asia and Pacific Region here.
Norazman said a flight from Oman was diverted to KLIA this morning while another from Saudi Arabia was diverted yesterday.

Indonesia suspended operations at eight airports, including Jakarta’s main gateway Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau spread across parts of Java and Sumatra beginning last Friday.
About 170,000 passengers have been affected by flight cancellations so far.
f8b1cddf3070fc57: CYBERJAYA: The Rural and Regional Development Ministry will not spend beyond its government-approved allocation, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today.
"Has any ministry ever spent more than it was allocated? I indirectly answer the Treasury secretary-general's question.

"How much has been allocated? No budget is perfect. How could the ministry possibly spend beyond what was announced in the Budget speech or allocated to us?" he said in his speech at the opening of a strategic cooperation workshop involving the ministry's Rural Community Centres (PKD) and National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi).
Present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Deputy Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang.
Zahid said government spending must also take into account the need to prevent wastage.
"I know MCMC (the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission) has plenty of money. Even so, it must comply with Treasury instructions when spending it.
"Otherwise, Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din (the MCMC chairman) will lose his job sooner," he said.

On Wednesday, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican had denied that funds were being withheld for the ministry, saying payment delays arose because the ministry had nearly exhausted its annual allocation.
As of June, the ministry had spent RM1.9 billion of its approved RM2.1 billion allocation for rural-road projects this year.
The Finance Ministry said an additional RM300 million had been approved to help settle outstanding payments.
The ministry subsequently denied claims that it had made unilateral financial commitments or spent as it pleased.
Its press secretary, Fadzmel Fadzil, said project approvals and allocations were subject to established government procedures.
Fadzmel also cited contractual commitments dating back to 2019 to 2021, when acceptance letters were issued for rural projects despite disruptions during the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said the RM300 million released remained insufficient to settle all outstanding contractor claims.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has since urged the Finance Ministry and KKDW to resolve the rural-road project payment issues amicably.
Meanwhile, Zahid said the ministry's success should not be measured solely by the number of programmes held, participants involved or funds spent.
He said more meaningful measures were how many young people secured employment, how many entrepreneurs increased their sales and how many families improved their incomes.
bb093ef300d79520: SINGAPORE, Sept 7 — Singapore Airlines (SIA) cancelled 19 flights between Singapore and Jakarta scheduled for yesterday, following volcanic activity caused by the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau in Indonesia.
In an advisory posted on its Facebook page SIA said all affected flights were scheduled to operate between Changi Airport and Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
“As the situation remains fluid, other SIA flights between Singapore and Indonesia may be affected.
“Customers may visit our Flight Status page for the latest information on their flights,” it said yesterday.
Meanwhile, SIA budget airline, Scoot also cancelled 12 flights scheduled for yesterday as a precautionary measure following the eruption.
The airline has reached out to affected customers via the contact details provided to inform them of the changes to their flights.

Anak Krakatau, which has been erupting since Friday, caused volcanic ash to spread, resulting in six major airports in Indonesia, including Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, being temporarily closed yesterday. — Bernama
caa2c4cfddf9d678: PARIS: Another UEFA Champions League season gets going this week with the beginning of the league phase as Paris Saint-Germain bid to join the tiny band of clubs to have won the competition three years running.
PSG successfully defended their title last season when they beat Arsenal on penalties in Budapest, retaining the trophy they won for the first time in their history 12 months earlier.

Luis Enrique's side have already secured their status as one of the competition's greatest teams by winning it back-to-back, something only Real Madrid had previously achieved since the inception of the modern Champions League in 1992.

Winning three in a row would be on another level entirely. Real did exactly that under Zinedine Zidane between 2016 and 2018, The only other teams to manage such a feat are Ajax (1971-73) and Bayern Munich (1974-76), while Madrid also won the first five editions of the European Cup from 1956 to 1960.
"Our objectives are clear. I want to win important trophies and there are none more important than the Champions League," said Luis Enrique, who also led Barcelona to glory in 2015.

The back-to-back titles for the French giants have coincided with the introduction of the new Champions League format, with 36 teams in the league phase now playing eight games against eight different opponents.
The Parisians struggled in the league phase in each of the last two campaigns, finishing outside the top eight and having to come through the additional play-off round to make the last 16.
Tough draws were partly responsible for that, and PSG will face some familiar opponents this time in Manchester City, Barcelona and Aston Villa.
With each passing year, the prospect of a team other than one of Europe's super clubs winning the Champions League seems more remote.
- Arsenal to take next step? -
The Premier League's financial strength means all of its representatives can be expected to feature prominently, with Arsenal chief among them.
Over the last three years, the Gunners have lost in the quarter-finals, the semi-finals, and then the final. There is therefore a logical next step for Mikel Arteta's side,
Arsenal topped the league phase last season with a perfect record. They have a tough start this time away to Napoli.
There are five English clubs involved, with Manchester City and Liverpool joined by the returning Manchester United and Villa.

Bayern Munich are formidable, while Jose Mourinho has returned to Real Madrid charged with the task of leading them back to continental glory. Barcelona are itching to get their hands on the trophy again.
It is hard to see beyond one of those clubs, although Inter Milan could have a say and Atletico Madrid will be desperate to reach a final to be held in their stadium.
- Debutants -
The only club outside Spain, England, Germany, Italy and France to have won the Champions League in the last 30 years remains Mourinho's Porto in 2004.
Plenty of new names will add freshness to the competition, including Como, who finished fourth in Serie A last season under Cesc Fabregas to qualify at the expense of AC Milan and Juventus.
Viking Stavanger are in the Champions League proper for the first time after winning a first Norwegian title in 34 years.

Sabah start with a trip to Old Trafford after winning a first Azerbaijani title and coming through four qualifying ties. Their manager, Valdas Dambrauskas, got into coaching with the money he made appearing on the Lithuanian version of 'Who Wants to be a Millionaire'.
"Since I was 12, when I realised I will not be a professional player, I knew I wanted to be a football coach," he said in an interview with Flashscore.
"I cannot guess what would have happened without this game, but I believe I would have found a way to achieve my dream."

Sabah might not qualify for the next stage – although compatriots Qarabag did that last season – but just being in the league phase is worth almost 20 million euros ($23.2m) at a minimum, significant sums for clubs from lesser leagues.

The Champions League winners pocket around 90 million euros in prize money, before adding millions more, notably from television – it is understood PSG earned around 150 million euros for each of their last two victories. - AFP

6b572bf95be3e344: BATU PAHAT: Johor will close schools if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 200, making it the second state after Selangor to adopt the threshold amid worsening air quality.
Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said all districts recorded unhealthy API readings yesterday, prompting the state to step up monitoring.
"We have discussed this with the state education department, and if the reading exceeds 200, the school session will be closed," he said after visiting SMK Suria Jaya in Parit Yaani today.
He said district education offices and schools were instructed to keep API data updated and ensure information reaches parents promptly, as readings could change throughout the day.
Dr Naqib said existing standard operating procedures allow schools to restrict outdoor activities when air quality is unsuitable.
"If necessary, we reduce outdoor activities. We are facing hot weather and must take this seriously," he said.
He urged parents to monitor API readings, ensure their children wear face masks outdoors, and provide sufficient drinking water to school during the haze and hot, dry weather.
The Education Ministry's existing guidelines require educational institutions to suspend outdoor activities, including assemblies and sports, when API readings exceed 100.
a5a647293027f962: GEORGE TOWN: Kelantan, Perak, Negri Sembilan and Pahang should reverse their decisions and adopt amendments aimed at strengthening protection of permanent reserved forests (PRFs), Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM) said.
SAM president Meenakshi Raman said the four states should not reject provisions aimed at enhancing public participation, transparency and forest conservation.
She said Article 76 of the Federal Constitution empowered parliament to legislate on matters under state jurisdiction in certain circumstances, including to promote uniformity of laws.
Meenakshi said the National Forestry Act 1984 (NFA 1984) was enacted on this basis for application by states in Peninsular Malaysia before being adopted through their respective state enactments.
She said amendments passed by parliament in 2022 introduced stricter requirements for the degazettement of PRFs, particularly through amendments to Sections 11 and 12.
Section 11 requires public participation before a PRF can be degazetted, while Section 12 requires a degazetted PRF to be replaced simultaneously with a new PRF of an equivalent or larger area.

"These two sections are introduced to prevent our forestry resources from being freely exploited without considering public interest, the rights of communities and the ecological and biological functions of a PRF proposed for degazettement," she said.
Meenakshi said SAM was disappointed by reports that the four states had decided not to adopt the two provisions despite accepting other amendments to the NFA.

She said the decision appeared to undermine the spirit of legal uniformity under Article 76 and denied citizens in those states the same protections enjoyed by people in states adopting the amendments in full.
"This is unfair and unjust. It contravenes Article 8 on equality of all citizens and their equal protection of the law of the Federal Constitution," she said.

Meenakshi also rejected Pahang's argument that its decision was based on state jurisdiction over land and forests, saying the issue was not about jurisdiction but better governance and forest protection.
She urged the federal government to strengthen mechanisms, including criteria for Ecological Fiscal Transfer allocations, to encourage states to support national conservation objectives.
"Ultimately, our action to protect the forest is also an action to protect the people," she added.
Meenakshi called on the four states to reverse course and adopt the amendments, saying public participation and stronger PRF protection should not be feared.
a8476244ad0139e8: BEIJING: Badminton world number one An Se-young sent a warning for the Asian Games as she clinched her third China Masters title in a row in ominous fashion.
South Korea's reigning Olympic and world champion will defend her crown when the Asian Games begin on Sept 19 in Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.
The 24-year-old will be overwhelming favourite after winning the China Masters on Sunday with a ruthless 21-17, 21-6 demolition of Tomoka Miyazaki in Shenzhen.
An did not drop a game all week on the way to her seventh title of the season.
"I'm so proud of myself. I'm really pleased with the result and I feel so happy," An said.
Despite being the undoubted dominant force in women's badminton once more this year, An said: "There are many players coming up and challenging.
"I don't think any match can be taken lightly."
The men's singles final was surprisingly an all-Hong Kong affair, with world number 32 Jason Gunawan defeating Lee Cheuk-Yiu 21-9, 21-16.
In the men's doubles, India's Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty beat home duo He Jiting and Ren Xiangyu in a three-game battle.
Shetty and Rankireddy will defend their Asian Games men's doubles title in Japan.
"Going into the Asian Games winning a title definitely reassures us what we are working on is heading in the right direction," said Shetty.
"We will go back home, push ourselves to the limit, train for the next 10 days and go all guns blazing in Japan. We want to go out there and have some fun."
China's Feng Yanzhe and Huang Dongping won the mixed doubles while Sumire Nakade and Miyu Takahashi of Japan clinched the women's doubles crown.
07233f15cd09586a: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Penerangan PAS Ahmad Fadhli Shaari mempersoalkan tindakan pemimpin Pakatan Harapan (PH) yang membuat laporan polis berhubung dakwaan Presiden Hadi Awang kononnya Amerika Syarikat (AS) pernah menawarkan bantuan menjatuhkan kerajaan Malaysia pada 2014.
Ahli Parlimen Pasir Mas itu berkata isu berkenaan pada asasnya melibatkan dua pihak utama iaitu Hadi dan Kedutaan AS di Malaysia yang telah pun menafikan dakwaan itu.
Katanya, sekiranya timbul sebarang pertikaian atau perbezaan kenyataan antara kedua-dua pihak, saluran undang-undang yang sivil adalah kaedah terbaik bagi menyelesaikan isu berkenaan.
"Apa yang menghairankan, kenapa tiba-tiba Pakatan Harapan (PH) melatah? Apa kepentingan mereka dalam isu ini?
"Adakah presiden PAS mengaitkan mana-mana pihak dari PH dalam isu ini? Tidak sekali-kali,” katanya di Facebook.

Semalam, tiga laporan polis dibuat dibuat Naib Ketua PKR Bandar Tun Razak V Jonathan, Ketua Wanita PKR Bandar Tun Razak Mazlina Osman dan Timbalan Ketua Pemuda PKR Bandar Tun Razak, Amarul Hisham Jalil, di Balai Polis Cheras terhadap kenyataan tersebut.
Hadi pada Muktamar Tahunan PAS Ke-72, Sabtu lalu mendakwa parti itu pernah ditawarkan pihak asing untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan ketika lawatan bekas presiden AS, Barack Obama ke Malaysia pada 2014.
Menurut Hadi, Takiyuddin Hassan dan Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar yang merupakan setiausaha politiknya ketika itu pergi ke kedutaan berkenaan bagi mengadakan pertemuan.
Bagaimanapun, perkara itu kemudian dinafikan Kedutaan AS di Kuala Lumpur dengan menegaskan negara itu tidak pernah berusaha untuk menentukan siapa yang memimpin Malaysia.
c39487d38ade57a2: KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department is ready to deploy its Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (Storm) team and mountain guides if needed in the search and rescue (SAR) operation for six people, including a family of four, feared missing after entering a forested area in Gua Musang on Aug 29.
Its director, Farhan Sufyan Borhan, said the SAR operation was being led by the Perak Fire and Rescue Department.
"We are on standby and will deploy four Storm personnel, four personnel from the Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station and six mountain guides from Gua Musang.
"If necessary, we will send them in as we are also concerned that the group may turn back towards Gua Musang," he said when contacted.
He said, however, that all six, including the 9-year-old child, were believed to have entered Perak on Sept 1.
"The group was said to have encountered another group of hikers last Tuesday, when the six were located at Gunung Bieh, Bilah, which is already within Perak," he said.
Earlier, media reported that six people, comprising a family of four and two mountain guides, were feared missing after entering the forest through Pos Dakoh, Lojing, Gua Musang, on Aug 29.

Gua Musang district police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo had said that police received a missing persons report from the group's family members in Selangor after they failed to emerge from the forest as scheduled on Sept 3.

The group had obtained a permit to enter the forest and was scheduled to exit through Pos Kemar in Perak, while Gua Musang police remained on standby should there be confirmation that they were in Kelantan.
f71b24c1c62e9150: MADRID: When Jose Mourinho left Inter Milan for Real Madrid in the summer of 2010, after leading the Italian outfit to Champions League glory, he was at the peak of his powers.
The Portuguese coach claimed an historic treble with Inter, clinching Serie A in the last week of the season and lifting the Coppa Italia.
Inter beat Bayern 2-0 in the Champions League final at Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu stadium, winning the trophy for the first time since 1965 and becoming the first Italian team to win the treble.
The day after the final Mourinho said it was likely his last match in charge and around a week later his appointment at Real Madrid was finalised.
Now 16 years on, and beginning his second stint at Madrid, Mourinho kicks off the record 15-time Champions League winners' European campaign against Inter on Tuesday at the Bernabeu.
Neither the veteran coach nor Inter have been able to reproduce that level of European success since.
Inter have reached the final on two subsequent occasions, beaten in 2023 by Manchester City and then thrashed by Paris Saint-Germain in the 2025 showpiece.
Mourinho was unable to help Real Madrid past the semi-finals and after leaving the club in 2013 has mainly spent his time competing in lower levels of European competition.
The 63-year-old led Manchester United to the Europa League in 2017 and won the Conference League with Roma in 2022.
- Back on top -

Fished out of the relative wilderness by Madrid president Florentino Perez this summer after two seasons without a major trophy for Los Blancos, Mourinho's main task is to return the club to their European throne.
Only five coaches have won the trophy more times than Mourinho, who also lifted it with Porto in 2004 to kickstart his career and earn him passage to Chelsea and Europe's biggest leagues.

"My attraction to Real Madrid is due to its history, its frustrations in recent years and its expectations to win," said Mourinho in 2010, although the same holds true now, after a remarkable period of success ended.
In his first reign Mourinho helped disrupt Pep Guardiola's Barcelona's dominance within Spain but was unable to help Madrid end their wait for a 10th European Cup.
That came under his successor Carlo Ancelotti, who claimed three with Madrid over two spells at the club.
Zinedine Zidane also lifted the trophy three times in consecutive seasons, with Madrid winning six in a remarkable 10-year spell.
Perez credits Mourinho with building the foundations for those trophies.
"I'm glad my work had some positive impact, but the titles belong to Carlo, Zidane, the players, and the fans," said Mourinho.
Madrid's grip on the trophy has loosened during the past two years, knocked out in the quarter-finals by Arsenal in 2025 and last season they were eliminated by Bayern Munich in the last 16.
Mourinho's challenge is to prove both he and Real Madrid still can rule among Europe's elite, and stopping Luis Enrique's PSG retaining it for a third year running.
"Finishing without trophies at Real Madrid is not a successful season," said Mourinho in August.
The coach's second stint at Madrid started smoothly with three wins from three games, but on Friday they fell to their first defeat, 1-0 at Real Betis.

Inter's visit to the Spanish capital will be an early test of whether Mourinho can restore Madrid's European fortunes, against the club with which he last reached the pinnacle of the competition. - AFP

06b30d885d9bbbdd: JAKARTA, Sept 7 — What was meant to be a week-long honeymoon in Bali turned into an unexpected ordeal for a young Malaysian couple after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau disrupted their journey home, leaving them stranded in Indonesia for five extra days with limited funds.

Amir Hamzah, 29, a factory worker from Kedah, and his wife, Fatin Zulaikha Azizal, also 29, who works for a private company, flew from Bali’s I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport at 8.40pm on Saturday to Jakarta for their 8.30am connecting flight to Kuala Lumpur the next morning.

Amir and his wife were due to return to Malaysia on Sunday but found themselves stuck at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after their connecting flight to Kuala Lumpur was repeatedly delayed and eventually cancelled.

“We thought we would just sleep at the airport for a few hours and then take the morning flight home. We never thought we would end up being stuck here for days,” Amir, who was travelling overseas for the first time, told Bernama.
They had already cleared immigration when the departure information screen showed their flight was delayed, with the departure time pushed back several times before it was eventually cancelled.

The disruption came as volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau forced Indonesian authorities to temporarily close Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and seven other airports, affecting about 150,000 passengers and 467 flights as of Sunday night.
After spending almost 24 hours at Soekarno-Hatta, the couple were informed by Garuda Indonesia that the earliest available flight was on Friday, Sept 11 — five days after their scheduled return.
“When I saw Friday, I was like, ‘Friday? What are we going to do here for another five days?’ We only prepared enough money for our honeymoon and to go home on Sunday,” he said.
He said buying replacement tickets would cost considerably more, while a refund for their cancelled flight would take several days to process.
“We were not told about any compensation, and from what we understood, there would be no compensation because the cancellation was due to force majeure.

“We had just got married, so of course, during the honeymoon we spent a bit more. We initially booked a budget hotel near the airport, but when we started calculating the cost of accommodation and food for another five days, we became worried that the money we had left would not be enough,” he said.

Concerned about how they would manage, Amir contacted Bernama’s Jakarta correspondent for assistance, and the couple were subsequently given temporary accommodation while waiting for help from their family in Malaysia.

Meanwhile, in Malaysia, 31 Jakarta-bound flights scheduled throughout Sunday were cancelled following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta, including 21 at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, according to Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd.

Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, began erupting at 11.07pm local time on Friday, with Indonesian authorities reporting volcanic ash reaching about 6,000 metres on the Java side and plumes of up to 15,000 metres towards Sumatra and parts of Banten province. — Bernama
a9fe47570130b586: DHAKA: Bangladesh's dengue outbreak is accelerating, with 42,590 people hospitalised and 117 deaths recorded this year, as a sharp September surge strains hospitals and raises fears the mosquito-borne disease could intensify further in the coming weeks.
At least four dengue patients died and 1,558 others were hospitalised in the past 24 hours, according to health ministry data, marking the highest daily admission tally recorded so far this year.

The disease, which can cause fever, severe headaches and potentially fatal complications, has spread sharply in recent weeks, reviving concerns after Bangladesh's deadliest dengue outbreak in 2023. The outbreak has further strained a healthcare system already grappling with a nationwide measles outbreak that has killed nearly 1,000 children this year.
Health experts warn September could prove even more severe than August, which recorded the highest monthly dengue caseload of the year.

Professor Kabirul Bashar, a medical entomologist at Jahangirnagar University, said his surveillance and forecasting model suggests hospitalisations could exceed 30,000 this month if current trends continue, with weather conditions likely to support transmission into October.
"The peak has not been reached yet," Bashar said. "If the current trajectory continues, September may become the worst month of the year for dengue infections."
For Zahid Hasan, 32, the outbreak became a personal ordeal when his four-year-old son developed a high fever and was diagnosed with dengue.
As the child's condition worsened, Hasan took him to three government hospitals but could not find an available bed.
"I was terrified. As a father, it was unbearable to watch my child getting worse without knowing where he could be admitted," Hasan said.
He eventually secured a bed at a private hospital with the help of a relative. His son received seven bags of blood and plasma before being discharged.
"Those days were a nightmare for us. We were constantly afraid something could happen to him," Hasan said. His son remains weak and is recovering slowly.

Dengue patients can deteriorate rapidly after their fever subsides, developing complications such as plasma leakage, low blood pressure, shock and severe bleeding, making close monitoring during the critical post-fever phase essential.

"Patients are flooding hospitals, and warning signs such as abdominal pain, dizziness and unusual lethargy must not be ignored," said Professor Tarek Alam, a physician treating dengue patients in Dhaka.

Bashar said the spread of Aedes mosquitoes beyond Dhaka and other major cities was fuelling infections in districts and rural areas. Dengue cases have now been reported in all 64 districts, although the capital continues to account for the largest share.

The government has intensified prevention efforts as the outbreak worsens. Prime minister Tarique Rahman has ordered nationwide cleanup and awareness campaigns, urging people to remove stagnant water and other mosquito-breeding sites while encouraging greater community participation in mosquito-control measures.

"Fogging alone cannot control dengue if breeding sites remain untouched," Bashar said. "Control efforts must target areas where Aedes mosquitoes are actually breeding. The biggest weakness in dengue control is the lack of evidence-based interventions."
04da0637162f4ff5: SHAH ALAM: Student enrolment in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) must be further strengthened, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said there remained a gap between students' interest in STEM and their readiness to pursue the field in greater depth, with participation in pure sciences currently at about 15.8 per cent.
"The issue is not only encouraging more students to choose STEM. We must also ensure that they continue, develop and succeed in the field," he said.
Anwar said this in his speech read by Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang at the closing of the National Science Challenge 2026 here today.
The finance minister said the government, schools, universities, industry and communities needed to work together to identify young talent, guide them and provide opportunities for them to develop.
"In this regard, teachers play a very important role, not merely as providers of knowledge, but as catalysts for curiosity and builders of confidence among the younger generation," he said.
He said opportunities to develop STEM talent should be available to every Malaysian child regardless of where they were born, which school they attended or their family background.
"Talent is everywhere. Our responsibility is to ensure opportunities are everywhere too, while efforts to strengthen STEM education must be a shared responsibility," he said.
Anwar said Education Ministry data showed student enrolment in STEM had increased from 40.95 per cent in 2021 to 50.83 per cent in 2024.
He described the increase as encouraging but said the country could not stop there.

He said students with potential, particularly those from rural areas, Sabah and Sarawak and lower-income families, should continue to be connected with mentors, laboratories, scholarships and innovation networks.
He said the National Science Challenge should serve as a continuous talent-development pathway rather than an annual competition that ended after the presentation of a trophy.
Anwar said Malaysia needed a stronger STEM talent pipeline to support research, innovation and technological development.
He said the country must also continue strengthening an ecosystem that gave young people opportunities to develop through universities, research institutions, industry and start-up companies.

"We want ideas born in schools today to develop into research, technology, innovation and enterprises that can solve real problems faced by the people and enhance Malaysia's competitiveness at the global level."
8c21d7a5815f6fe9: BATU PAHAT: A school project classified as a "sick project" finally opened its doors today, 11 years after it was originally scheduled for completion.
Construction of SMK Suria Jaya began in 2013 and was initially scheduled for completion in June 2015.

Although the project had reached 97 per cent physical progress by 2020, it remained unfinished after the contractor failed to complete critical works, including utility connections and an access road, as well as secure the necessary approvals.
The contractor was subsequently terminated, with a new contractor appointed to undertake rehabilitation works in 2023.
Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali, said the opening marked an important milestone for the Parit Yaani community after years of waiting.
"The new school building is the fulfilment of a long-awaited education facility closer to the community," he said during a working visit to the school today.
He said the school would provide easier access to secondary education for students from Parit Yaani, Sri Medan, Yong Peng and surrounding areas.
SMK Suria Jaya opened with 221 pupils from Forms One to Three, comprising 76 Form One, 70 Form Two and 75 Form Three pupils.
Naqib said the school currently had nine of its 30 classrooms in use, with a maximum capacity of 900 pupils.
The school is staffed by 21 teachers, including eight administrators and 13 academic teachers, supported by five support staff.
"After such a long wait, what matters now is ensuring this facility is fully utilised for the benefit of the children and community," he said.
He said the experience should also serve as a lesson for future development projects, particularly in contractor performance, progress monitoring and the swift resolution of implementation issues.
"The school may have taken a long journey to be built, but its future begins today," he said.
fff04813aa84c9b0: LOS ANGELES: Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is unlikely to pitch again this season, team manager Dave Roberts said Sunday.
The Japanese has suffered multiple injuries, missing four consecutive games this week for the first time since he joined the Dodgers in 2023.
Ohtani has not pitched in a game since July 3. He has battled inflammation and soreness, and experienced injury setbacks after bullpen throwing sessions.
Roberts on Sunday expressed hope that Ohtani could return to the Dodgers' batting lineup as soon as Monday.
But with just three weeks remaining of the regular season, Roberts downplayed the prospect of Ohtani returning to the mound as a full-fledged starter this year.
"Obviously if you're looking at the calendar, how much he's thrown in the last week, I think we can all do the math," said Roberts.
Asked if Ohtani might instead throw just an inning at a time as an opener, Roberts responded: "I think that's unlikely."
Ohtani has played a crucial role as the Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series the past two seasons, but his pitching role has been limited.
After undergoing two right elbow operations in 2023, Ohtani did not take the mound at all for the Dodgers until last June.
After a rehab-free off-season, this was meant to be the year Ohtani returned as a full-time two-way player, with the Japanese star targeting the Cy Young Award for outstanding pitching.
But that has been derailed by injuries to his left knee, right biceps and neck.
Ohtani's batting form has slumped in recent weeks as he has attempted to return as a pitcher.
c7d9a361469a0e6c: BARCELONA, Sept 7 — Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 yesterday to maintain their 100 per cent start in La Liga.
The reigning champions moved two points clear at the top of La Liga, after Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.
Unbeaten Alaves rose to second place with a thumping 5-2 victory over Osasuna.
As well as Yamal, Fermin Lopez, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick’s swaggering Barca on a hot afternoon on Spain’s east coast.
Yamal did not take part in the team training session on Saturday after a knock but showed no signs of it during a dazzling display against Carlos Corberan’s side.

Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia’s fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium. Los Che are bottom and yet to win this season.
“We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team,” said Flick.
“We stay calm and then if it’s possible to score, we try to do it — it was a fantastic game for us.
“Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it’s perfect then you can stop working.”
Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Lopez dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star.
The 19-year-old slammed home at the near post for what he thought was Barca’s second goal but the goal was disallowed for a tight offside after a VAR review.
Lopez netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up.

Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric Garcia had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with team-mate Rodri’s shoulder, on the midfielder’s first start since arriving this summer from Manchester City.
Yamal fired narrowly wide and Lopez struck the post as Flick’s side continued to dominate. Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia made a smart save to thwart Arnaut Danjuma at his near post before the break.
Raphinha, starting again as the team’s centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Lopez fed him.
Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona’s fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo.
A long way to go
New arrival Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barca debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide.
Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barca’s fifth and conclude a profitable afternoon for both the World Cup winner and the Catalan giants.

“We have a very young team, with the right transfers we made, but it’s the beginning of the season, it’s not the end,” added Flick, telling his team not to get too excited yet about their strong start.
“We have to go a long, long way.”
Corberan said his team were up against it from the start after Yamal’s rapid strike.
“Conceding a goal so early, on their first or second attack, made everything much more difficult,” said the Valencia coach.
“It’s a difficult situation that we will navigate together.”
Later on Sunday Lucas Boye bagged a hat-trick for Alaves as they crushed Osasuna 5-2, with two of his efforts coming from long range.
Former Real Madrid striker Mariano Diaz and Pablo Ibanez also scored for Quique Sanchez Flores’s team, while Ante Budimir grabbed two for Osasuna, who fell to their first defeat.
“I hope we don’t take our foot off the gas and we stay in this dynamic, which will take us far,” said Boye.
“This is a humble team and we will go game by game.” — AFP
2539138619c19acb: BELGRADE: Convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic is to be buried in Belgrade on Monday at a ceremony expected to draw thousands despite international condemnation.
Mladic died in late August aged 84 while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the 1990s war in Bosnia.
His body will be displayed in a church for five hours before a ceremony and a procession to a nearby cemetery.
His casket was flown to Serbia on Thursday aboard a government plane, draped in national flags and welcomed with military honours.
As it was driven from the airport, mostly young men gathered on motorway overpasses, displaying banners honouring Mladic and lighting flares, while some police officers were seen saluting the convoy.
Backlash

The European Union enlargement commissioner, Marta Kos, cancelled a forthcoming visit to Serbia, saying the "glorification surrounding his death is incompatible with the values on which the EU path is built".
Denis Becirovic, chairman of Bosnia's tripartite presidency, called it "an act of identification by Serbia's leadership with one of the worst killers in European history".
"This has unforeseeable consequences for the future of the entire region," he wrote on Facebook on Friday.
Mladic's wartime atrocities during the break-up of the former Yugoslavia earned him the nickname "Butcher of Bosnia" in international media.
The 1992-1995 war left around 100,000 people dead and displaced 2.2 million.
Mladic was the military figurehead of the Bosnian Serb leadership alongside former Yugoslav president Slobodan Milosevic and Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic.
The United Nations war crimes court convicted him of genocide over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, where Bosnian Serb forces killed around 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys in a UN-protected safe zone.
The atrocity was Europe's worst act of bloodshed since World War II.
Fadila Efendic, whose son and husband were killed in Srebrenica, told AFP earlier that it pained her "to know that his ideas are not dead".

Mladic was also convicted of persecuting and forcibly expelling Bosnian Muslims and Croats, terrorising civilians during the siege of Sarajevo and taking UN peacekeepers hostage during Nato air strikes in 1995.
Hero
Mladic was arrested in 2011, 16 years after he was first indicted, and sentenced to life in prison in 2021 after a nine-year trial.
Despite the verdicts, he is still hailed as a hero by some Serbs, particularly in Bosnia's Serb statelet, Republika Srpska, where his death was marked with vigils and gatherings.
Many from the entity have applied to travel to Belgrade for the funeral.
Mladic's son Darko, who is officially organising the funeral, said he was "proud of the role" played by his father.
On Saturday, around 300 people gathered at a commemoration for Mladic at a military facility in Belgrade, organised by an association of retired and active Serbian army generals.
Darko and other family members also attended, as well as Serbian Justice Minister Nenad Vujic and officials from Republika Srpska, including President Sinisa Karan.
Speakers at the ceremony praised Mladic's wartime role, describing him as a "towering figure both as a man and a soldier".
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said that tens of thousands of people were expected to attend the funeral and that the state would ensure the event passed "safely".
He would not attend in person due to a prior engagement, he explained.

a5952ad501b78177: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — The Penang government will auction a 2.42-hectare plot of land in Tanjung Pinang next month to help Consortium Zenith Construction Sdn Bhd (CZC) secure the cash flow needed to complete the remaining works on the Ayer Itam-Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway bypass project.

State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the state agreed to auction the land after CZC sought assistance to monetise it and obtain the cash flow needed to complete the project by April 2027.
The freehold plot is located at P.T. 858 (Plot 7A), Seksyen 2, Bandar Tanjung Pinang in the northeast district of the island.

“The bypass project is funded not through cash payments to the contractor, but through a land-swap method, where land plots are transferred based on completed work claims,” Zairil said in a statement today.
He said CZC had so far claimed land worth RM695.977 million for completed works.
Of that amount, 4.7ha (11.6183 acres) of land worth RM427.657 million had been transferred to the company, he said.
“Therefore, RM225.768 million in claimed land value had yet to be transferred,” he said.
The project, which links Ayer Itam to the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway, was about 92.46 per cent complete as of August 31, while its financial progress stood at 81.69 per cent, he said.
Zairil said the land, located beside Gurney Bay and Pulau Andaman, has a reserve price of RM313.632 million, or RM1,200 per square foot.
“It will be auctioned at 11am on October 7 at Level 51, Komtar,” he said.
“Profits from the sale will be shared between the state government and CZC,” he added.
Interested bidders must submit a bank draft deposit of RM3,136,320, or one per cent of the reserve price, payable to the District Land Administrator before 11am on the auction day.
Further information is available from the appointed auction agent, One Asia Property Consultants (PG) Sdn Bhd at 25-F Gottlieb Road, 10350 Pulau Pinang, or by calling +604-227 7222.
Participation in the auction is fully subject to the terms and conditions set out in the Proclamation of Sale issued by the Penang state authority.
3107942dfbcc4e85: KUALA LUMPUR: Puteri Umno bimbang pekerjaan gig yang sepatutnya menjadi sumber pendapatan sampingan dianggap sebagai pekerjaan utama dalam kalangan anak muda.
Ketua Puteri Umno, Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi, berkata ada graduan berkelulusan tinggi terpaksa bergantung pada pekerjaan gig selepas gagal mendapatkan pekerjaan yang bersesuaian dengan kelayakan.
"Pekerjaan gig tidak sepatutnya menjadi jawapan utama kepada anak muda yang mempunyai ijazah tetapi tidak mendapat pekerjaan yang sesuai.
"Saya nak tekankan kerajaan ambil serius mengenai ini," katanya kepada FMT ketika ditemui di Pejabat Puteri Umno, Menara Tun Hussein Onn.

Pemantauan Ekonomi Malaysia April 2026 oleh Bank Dunia, bertajuk 'Menaikkan Siling, Menaikkan Lantai: Agenda Pekerjaan sebagai Agenda Produktiviti', melaporkan sektor gig kini menjadi antara entiti yang memacu guna tenaga rakyat Malaysia.

Menurut laporan Berita Harian pada 25 Mei itu, data menunjukkan jumlah platform pekerjaan digital berdaftar dengan Perbadanan Ekonomi Digital Malaysia meningkat daripada 11 pada 2016 kepada 123 pada 2021, melibatkan anggaran 1.12 juta pekerja gig.
Menurut Bank Dunia, 31% pekerja gig sepenuh masa menyatakan mereka memasuki sektor itu kerana gagal memperoleh pekerjaan formal yang bersesuaian.
Katanya lagi, sebanyak 34% daripada pekerja gig yang gagal mendapatkan pekerjaan formal adalah pemegang ijazah atau pendidikan tertiari.
Nurul Amal berkata kerajaan perlu menyediakan lebih banyak peluang pekerjaan yang mampu menawarkan kestabilan serta prospek kerjaya untuk jangka panjang.
Kerajaan juga perlu mewujudkan pekerjaan atau memperkukuh sektor yang sepadan dengan bidang pengajian yang menghasilkan jumlah graduan paling tinggi, katanya.
"Kita kena pandang serius sebab benda ini meningkat hari demi hari dan orang muda semakin ramai," katanya.
Nurul Amal berkata isu ketidakpadanan antara kelayakan graduan dan peluang pekerjaan tidak boleh dililihat sebagai sekadar 'masalah semasa'.
"Bagaimana kita nak membentuk generasi akan datang dan membasmi benda-benda ini untuk 10 hingga 15 tahun akan datang," katanya.
02f765cf622f4a51: KUALA LUMPUR: Gig work should not be the main source of income for Malaysian youth, says Puteri Umno chief Nurul Amal Fauzi.
She said highly-qualified graduates were being forced to depend on gig work after failing to secure jobs that match their qualifications.

"Gig work should not be the ultimate answer for young people with degrees who are unable to find suitable employment. I want to push the government to take this seriously," she told FMT when met at the Puteri Umno office at Menara Tun Hussein Onn recently.
According to a recent World Bank report, the gig sector has become one of the drivers of employment in Malaysia.

The report, "Raising the Ceiling, Raising the Floor: The Jobs Agenda as a Productivity Agenda", said the number of digital job platforms registered with Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation increased from 11 in 2016 to 123 in 2021, with an estimated 1.12 million gig workers.
It also said that 31% of full-time gig workers said they entered the sector after failing to secure appropriate formal employment.
The report said 34% of gig workers who failed to secure formal employment were tertiary education graduates.

Nurul Amal said the government must provide more stable job opportunities with long-term career prospects and strengthen sectors that correspond with the fields of study producing the highest number of graduates.
She said the mismatch between graduate qualifications and employment opportunities could not be treated as a temporary issue.
"We must shape the next generation and eradicate this problem over the next 10 to 15 years," she said.
c89849624079dc73: TAIPEI: Taiwan flexed its chip diplomacy muscles at a major trade show last week, portraying itself as a democratic and reliable supplier for the AI revolution, while signalling a willingness to share the benefits of its semiconductor prowess with like-minded partners.

Home to companies like TSMC whose chips power AI applications, diplomatically isolated Taiwan has long sought to leverage its tech prowess to garner international support, something Beijing routinely seeks to block, saying the island is merely one of its provinces.

But Taiwan also faces pressure from the US, its most important international backer and arms supplier, to shift more chip manufacturing there. That comes as TSMC is investing US$265 billion in factories in the state of Arizona.

President Lai Ching-te, who, unusually, spoke at two separate events on the same day at the SEMICON Taiwan trade show, said Taiwanese companies were expanding globally to "let resilience create shared prosperity" and that the island's chip strength was based on democracy and rule of law.
Economy minister Kung Ming-hsin, opening the US pavilion at the show, said Taiwanese companies were planning an additional US$20 billion of investment in the country.
Taiwan struck a deal with Washington earlier this year to increase investment in the US in exchange for reduced export tariffs, but uncertainty remains.
US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick told CNBC last week that semiconductor tariffs were coming for companies that do not make chips in the US.
Still, Bill Frauenhofer, the commerce department official overseeing the tariff agreement with Taiwan, struck an upbeat tone during SEMICON.
"The phenomenal partnership" between Taiwan and the US was working, he said. "And we really, both of us, have vested interests in terms of making this successful."
Taiwanese firms acknowledge the need to expand manufacturing beyond the island.
Young Liu, chairman of Foxconn, Nvidia's largest AI server maker, said companies now had to "think about how to make with Taiwan, not in Taiwan; make with Taiwan in the country where the market is."
Responding to Liu during the panel discussion, Tien Wu, chief operating officer of ASE, the world's largest chip packaging ​and testing provider, said he agreed.
"Politically it is the right thing," Wu said. "And honestly, I don't think we have a choice not to do that."

Taiwan is also seeking to deepen ties with the EU, which likewise wants greater investment from Taiwanese companies. The bloc sent European Commission official Kilian Gross to SEMICON to pitch the bloc's Chips Act 2.0 to Taiwanese officials and companies.
Taiwan has sought closer cooperation with the EU not only because both have strongly backed Ukraine in the war with Russia, but also because both face trade and diplomatic disputes with China.

Deputy foreign minister Francois Wu, one of Taiwan's most prominent diplomats, told the opening of the French pavilion that Taiwan and France shared the values of democracy, freedom and a commitment to a rules-based international order.
"We use technology to connect with the world, not to control it," he added.
7ffca306eccf2705: MONZA, Sept 7 — Charles Leclerc admitted his opening-lap scrap with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton went “too far” before crashing out of yesterday’s Italian Grand Prix, leaving a vast scarlet-clad crowd disappointed.
The Monegasque driver clashed with Hamilton at the first chicane, where the Briton bounced into the gravel and dropped to 10th from fourth.
“Charles pushed me off,” moaned Hamilton on team radio.
Leclerc then slammed into the barriers at Parabolica on lap two and out of the race.
After the recent Dutch Grand Prix, Hamilton complained that that the team had not issued orders to Leclerc.
Yesterday, the Briton was asked if the team should have made him the priority over Leclerc in the battle with the Mercedes-powered rivals atop standings.

“It’s too far past that already, too late for that now and I lost a lot of points to those guys,” said Hamilton. “We will do our best to keep pushing the rest of the season, but they are out and out ahead of us.”
Leclerc said he suffered slight vision problems, but was more concerned at suggestions that the two Ferrari drivers appeared not to be working together as a team.
“I don’t really know who is forcing the narrative, that we are one against the other. At Zandvoort, there were way too many talks already,” he said.
“Here, it’s true though that we went too far, I think, with Lewis in Turn One.”
Hamilton came into the weekend hoping for a record sixth win to boost his slim hopes for an eighth title.
“That one hurts,” he said. “That one definitely hurts. Thank you to everyone. To the tifosi, thank you for giving us your love, I’m sorry we couldn’t give you the result you wanted.”

“I gave it absolutely everything, we just didn’t have the speed on the straights. I was just mostly a sitting duck to those guys around me and up ahead, but we will look internally and try and figure out what we could have done better.”
Leclerc was checked over at the circuit medical centre after his crash and said he would require more checks before next weekend’s first Spanish race at the new Madring circuit.
“I think I’ll have quite a few additional checks that we still have to do on my side probably tonight and tomorrow to make sure that I’ll be fully fine for Madrid,” he said.
“It should be the case, but better to be safe than sorry.” — AFP
eeba7777c9a4699f: JAKARTA, Sept 7 — When Anak Krakatau’s ash grounded flights across the region, seven stranded Malaysians found themselves with nowhere to go and dwindling patience.
A stranger’s spare bedroom changed that.
Maira Safiraa, an Indonesian who currently lives in Malaysia, opened up her Jakarta house to the group after watching the flight chaos unfold from afar.
“I thought to myself, what if I or my family were in the same situation in a foreign country?” she said in a post on Threads.
That question was enough for her to offer up her home, located about 30 minutes from the airport,
Three of her four bedrooms filled up quickly, and she says the last one is still open, with priority given to women travelling alone.
There is no catch and no bill waiting at the end of the stay.
“The accommodation is free... I am not asking for any payment,” she said.
Anak Krakatau has been erupting continuously since Friday, blanketing the region in ash and forcing six airports to shut their runways.
The fallout has rippled well beyond Indonesia, disrupting flights to Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul, Doha and Amsterdam.
Maira said the timing worked out — her house happened to be empty apart from her personal assistant, who now has company instead of an empty house to sit in alone.
“I’m actually happy that my home in Jakarta has become livelier with more people around,” she said.
Airport authorities have told her the disruptions are expected to persist until at least 12.30pm tomorrow, longer still if the volcano refuses to settle.

Her goodwill has limits she cannot help — she said she feels for Indonesians stuck in Malaysia in the same predicament, but has no space to return the favour, with her own household already full with her husband, baby and helper.
For now, her open door is one less thing seven Malaysians have to worry about while they wait out the ash.
3b90f96348e0866e: MONZA, Sept 7 — Kimi Antonelli had every reason to pinch himself yesterday after his spectacular triumph for Mercedes from 19th on the grid gave the Monza fans a first home winner of the Italian Grand Prix for 60 years.
As he battled his emotions, Antonelli, who only turned 20 two weeks ago, admitted on team radio that “it feels like a dream”.
His win was delivered from the most distant starting position since John Watson raced to victory for McLaren at the 1983 United States Grand Prix West in Long Beach from 22nd on the grid.
More pointedly, victory over teammate George Russell opens up a 66-point lead in the title race.
“It’s a dream come true,” he said. “What an incredible day. I couldn’t do this without my team, my family and everyone who supports me.”
He resisted the temptation, however, to talk about becoming the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
“There’s still a few races to go, so we will try to keep our heads down. But now, yes, we are going to enjoy today.
“I did not expect this. Unbelievable. Unbelievable. I am so happy. I could not have imagined to be here today, but we managed to pull it off and I am really, really happy.”
Antonelli did have one scare in the race, four laps from the end when he was trying to overtake Russell and found himself in the gravel.
“It was quite scary because the tarmac was breaking up, but I still thought I could do the corner.
“I went straight. I was thinking like maybe I lost my chance, but luckily, we had the pace and I could bring it home.”
Starting yesterday’s race from the back of the grid due to penalties after taking a new power unit, he said he had felt capable of winning after going from 19th to 12th in the opening laps.
Then Charles Leclerc crashed his Ferrari to bring a red-flag stoppage and a re-start.
“After the second re-start, I was up there and I knew I could have had a shot for the win. So definitely I believed in it, especially when I was behind George,” he said.

“But it was difficult to break away with it all being so strong. At the end we pitted, he stayed out and he struggled with his tyres at the end so with fresher tyres we could increase the pace and get the win.”
Russell ‘disappointed’
His Mercedes team-mate Russell was left to rue the moment that his teammate pitted while he remained out on track.
“In hindsight, it’s easy to say I should have pitted rather than stayed out,” he said.
“I felt like I was holding my own at that point, but I think that’s partly why the team wanted us to split strategies.
“I’m disappointed with missing out on the win but here we are.”
Triumphant team boss Toto Wolff had nothing but praise for Antonelli, the first home winner at Monza since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.
“It was unbelievable,” he said. “He was so controlled all race. He kept his head down, took no risks at the start and then one by one he passed them. An amazing drive.”
Russell added that he was not considering or worrying about the title race.
“We are where we are,” he said. “He (Antonelli) has driven incredibly this season. He deserves to lead the championship and he has a healthy lead.

“I’m not even going to think about the fight or the comeback. I’m just going to every race trying to win it. I’m not putting any pressure on myself in this regard. I just need to try and win more races.
“He is in the best spot and he deserves to be where he is.” — AFP

d866df7fa839c495: LIVERPOOL, Sept 7 — Ainsley Maitland-Niles marked his Everton debut with a superb strike with virtually the last kick of the game to snatch a 2-2 draw for the Toffees against Manchester United yesterday.
Maitland-Niles’s arrival from Lyon on the final day of the transfer window was overshadowed by Everton’s failure to reinforce their attack.
But the former Arsenal full-back lasered a long-range shot into the top corner in the 96th minute to punish a lacklustre United performance.
Bryan Mbeumo fired United in front inside the first minute of the second period.
But an Everton side short on attacking options rallied to level through Tyrique George.
Substitute Benjamin Sesko’s header looked to have won United all three points.
But the decision not to reinforce Michael Carrick’s defence will face more scrutiny as United have conceded twice in all of their opening three games of the Premier League season.
“It feels like a defeat,” said Carrick. “We’re bitterly disappointed to be up in the position we were in the game twice, so close to the end... it’s not a great feeling.”
A draw maintains Everton’s unbeaten start and keeps them one point ahead of United to calm the sense of unrest among the club’s fans.
“It was a brilliant goal and I thought it was a big moment for the crowd as well, I think it was good for them,” said Everton boss David Moyes.
A miserable end to the window could still have ramifications for Everton’s performance over the rest of the season.

After letting Iliman Ndiaye depart in a £65 million (US$88 million) move to Manchester City and Beto to leave for Fiorentina, the Toffees expected to strengthen their forward line with the signing of Monaco’s Folarin Balogun.
An issue with the USA international’s medical saw the clubs frantically renegotiate the structure of a £40 million deal but Balogun turned his back on the move.
Moyes has been left with only one natural striker to pick from in Thierno Barry as a result and only 18 outfield players.
The return of Jack Grealish on loan for the season only slightly softened the blow as Moyes faces up to the realities of a possible relegation battle rather than a challenge for European football.
Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick as United thrashed Ipswich 5-2 last weekend to get their season up and running after a dreadful 2-0 defeat at Hull.
The United captain came closest to breaking the deadlock in a first half otherwise devoid of quality when his volley came back off the crossbar.
Grealish return lifts home fans
A sleepy start to the second by Moyes’s men proved costly as Mbeumo was allowed to bear down on goal on his favoured left foot and arrow a shot beyond Jordan Pickford.
United, though, failed to build on their advantage and the introduction of Grealish off the bench lifted the home crowd.
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall twice failed to connect sweetly with clear sights of goal.
But the visitors’ luck ran out seven minutes from time when Hayden Hackney fed George and the former Chelsea winger blasted into the top corner from a narrow angle.
Sesko’s involvement has been limited at the start of the campaign due to an injury in pre-season, but the Slovenian looked sharp as he stooped to head in Luke Shaw’s cross to restore United’s lead.
The Red Devils never looked comfortable at the back but could not have foreseen the manner of the equaliser.
United looked to have cleared the danger with the five minutes of added time up, but the ball broke to Maitland-Niles who swept a curling shot into the top corner. — AFP
abcb97b5be59aa37: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump's name-changing spree found an unlikely new target on Sunday when he suggested the state of New Mexico could become "New America".

His proposal, which was immediately dismissed by the state's governor, comes days after he signed an order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America" in the middle of a trade war with neighbouring Canada.

"Many people suggested changing the name of New Mexico... to NEW AMERICA," the Republican president posted on social media. "So much more prestigious and beautiful for the people of that potentially incredible State. Wow, I Love It!!!"
The White House reposted an image showing the Mexico part of the state's name crossed out and replaced with "America".
Some US media reports said the idea originated as an internet hoax.
State governor Michelle Lujan Grisham told Fox News that the name "isn't up for debate – it's been ours since before the US existed."
She said the president wanted to "distract Americans" from issues such as soaring gas prices.
Trump last week suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz as "Trump Strait" as the war with Iran continues – then hours later implied he was not serious about the plan.
He renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America" on his first day back in the White House in 2025 in a move rejected by Mexico.
Canada has also rejected the attempt to rename Lake Ontario.
c07a3b0db18a828e: JAKARTA: Eight Indonesian airports, including two serving Jakarta, remained closed early on Monday morning because of volcanic ash from eruptions at Mount Anak Krakatau, the transport minister said.

Ash from Anak Krakatau, which sits halfway between Java and Sumatra islands, has blanketed Jakarta and several surrounding areas since it erupted late on Friday, leading to the closure of the airports for safety reasons.
The transport ministry said 170,000 people have been affected by flight cancellations.
Jakarta's main airport will remain closed until 6pm local time (1100 GMT), its operators said on Monday on Instagram.

"We cannot ascertain when this will end due to the dynamic weather," Transport minister Dudy Purwagandhi said in a statement on Monday, adding that the seven other airports, which included the ones serving Jakarta's nearby provinces of Lampung and West Java, would remain closed until at least 8.59am.
The volcano monitoring agency's website showed the most recent Anak Krakatau eruption occurred Sunday at 8.23pm.
The agency warned on Monday that "the probability of further eruptions in the coming periods remains high."

The eruptions have seen ash reach as high as 20,000 feet (6,000m) on the Java side of the volcano and 50,000 feet (15,000m) on the Sumatra side and some parts of Banten province in Java, meteorological agency BMKG posted on its website.

On Sunday, the disaster agency called for people to wear masks while travelling outdoors to avoid breathing in the ash. In Jakarta and Lampung, schools will use remote learning to counter health risks for students, state news agency Antara reported.
Indonesia sits on the Pacific "Ring of Fire", where earthquakes and volcanic eruptions are frequent.

Anak Krakatau, which means child of Krakatau, began emerging a century ago from the area previously occupied by Krakatau, then known as Krakatoa. The older volcano destroyed itself in mass eruptions in 1883, which killed more than 36,000 people in a series of tsunamis.
8066e464c94c08c1: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — A former Felda general manager was brought to the Magistrate’s Court here today to face remand proceedings in connection with an abuse of power investigation involving the appointment of a developer for a project in the capital, as well as the sale of land owned by the statutory body.
The man, in his late 60s, arrived at 9.15am in a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) vehicle, wearing a green collared shirt.
He was detained at 4pm yesterday together with a man in his 50s after they were asked to appear at the MACC headquarters here to have their statements recorded.
Last week, MACC opened seven investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).

MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman was reported as saying that the large-scale special investigation, ‘Ops Fella’, focused on investment transactions and asset acquisitions by the management of Felda and FIC over 10 years from 2010 to 2020.

Of the seven investigation papers, six new papers were opened on Aug 24, while the remaining one is an old investigation paper that remains active and is undergoing the Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) process.

The investigation papers cover issues involving the investment in Syarikat Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd, based in Limbang, Sarawak; the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah; and the purchase of Grand Plaza Service Apartments in London.

The investigation also focuses on the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd, the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House, as well as alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.
An old investigation paper involving the Park City Grand Plaza property, which remains open and is currently undergoing the MLA process, is also being reviewed in parallel. — Bernama
53ebc96a00e0ce79: NEW YORK: Eighth-seeded Ben Shelton overpowered former world number three Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday to book a US Open quarter-final date with defending champion Carlos Alcaraz.
Shelton – riding high after a strong August that included a title at the ATP Montreal Masters, where he didn't drop a set – dominated on serve.
The American blasted a dozen aces and never faced a break point in a match lasting just one hour and 52 minutes.
Shelton put 71% of his first serves in play and won 84% of those points.
"I was focused today," said Shelton, a 2023 US Open semi-finalist. "I played a complete match from start to finish."
Shelton powered through the opening set in 31 minutes, breaking Tsitsipas on the way to a 3-0 lead and breaking again to pocket the set.
He seized control of the second set with a break for 4-2, setting up his chance with a delicate drop shot to end another thumping baseline rally.
A forehand winner down the line had put Shelton up 5-2 when Tsitsipas called for the trainer.
He engaged in a lengthy conversation with the physio before receiving medication as Shelton became increasingly restive.
Tsitsipas then held at love, but Shelton was on the move again and closed out the set in the next game with an emphatic forehand winner.
He bagged another early break in the third set and cruised home.
Now he awaits Alcaraz, the seven-time Grand Slam champion who opted to make the US Open his first tournament back from a four-month injury layoff.
The Spaniard delivered his most convincing display of the tournament in a 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 victory over American Tommy Paul, and Shelton said it would take "special tennis" to beat him.
"I think the level that he's been playing at is really, really impressive," Shelton said. "I think it's going to be fireworks on Tuesday night."
It was a disappointing ending for Tsitsipas, a two-time Grand Slam finalist who hadn't made the second week of a major in more than two years.
The Greek has been in resurgent form this season, playing pain-free after battling back trouble last year.
b7cf57631d85b897: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Bursa Malaysia opened higher today, in line with the positive performance in some regional markets.
At 9.10 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 6.28 points, or 0.36 per cent, to 1,714.38 from Friday’s close of 1,708.10.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd equity research vice-president Thong Pak Leng said that despite the better performance, the benchmark index could continue to consolidate following the weaker Wall Street last Friday.
